Coefficient bundles and the projection formula

We first prove the coefficient-bundle identity on an actual tube and counting correspondence, then identify the ordinary graph construction with the zero-foliation case. The geometric inputs are the full DG-CHAR bundle and DG-FND unitary transport proofs linked above. The finite-module and analytic product inputs are Corollary6.0d, Lemmas6.0e–j/6.0n and Section0.

For a smooth Hermitian bundle \(E\to X\), write \(u_X(E)=[\Gamma_0(E),\mathrm{mult},0]\) as a class in \(KK(C_0(X),C_0(X))\), with \(E\) even. This notation makes sense also for noncompact \(X\). A countable relatively compact frame cover, its compact chart exhaustions and countable scalar coefficient approximations give a countable norm-dense set of sections. Finite chart partitions approximate any compact section in the supremum norm; compact cutoffs then approximate any section vanishing at infinity. The identity on a finite frame patch is a finite sum of section rank-one maps. A finite partition on a compact coefficient support makes multiplication by a nonnegative coefficient a finite sum of such maps, using the partition's square roots; linearity and approximation give all \(C_0(X)\) coefficients. Thus the module is countably generated, the left action is compact, and the zero-operator cycle is defined. It does not require a global finite trivialization on a noncompact space.

Bundle transport on the entire normalized tube

Lemma 6.0p. Let \(i:L\hookrightarrow X\) be a compact-source smooth embedding with the specified spin-c normal structure, of rank \(k\). The ambient manifold may be noncompact. For every smooth Hermitian \(E\to X\), there is an equality \[ u_L(i^*E)\,i_! =i_!\,u_X(E)^{[k]} \quad\text{in }KK(C(L),C_0(X)\widehat\otimes C_k). \tag{196} \] Here \(u_X(E)^{[k]}\) denotes its exterior extension by the identity on the retained \(C_k\). Both products are represented on the actual essential tube modules. The equality retains every twist of the prescribed normal orientation.

Proof. Choose the normalized whole-bundle tube \(\tau:\nu_i\to U\subset X\) of Lemma6.0e. Choose a Hermitian metric connection on \(E\). The exact DG-FND connection construction applies to its unitary frame bundle, using the already proved smooth bump partition; its associated transport is unitary. For each \((x,v)\in\nu_i\), transport from \(i(x)\) to \(\tau(x,v)\) along \(t\mapsto\tau(x,tv)\), \(0\leq t\leq1\). Denote the resulting unitary by \(T_{x,v}:E_{i(x)}\to E_{\tau(x,v)}\). This is defined on the entire normal bundle. For a fixed finite \(v\), its path is a compact smooth path on the full interval; the unitary transport ODE has no finite-time escape, by the full associated transport proof. Smooth parameter dependence on each compact family of \((x,v)\) follows from that same ODE argument, so \(T\) is a globally smooth bundle map. At \(v=0\) it is the identity.

Let \(\mathscr H_\nu\) be the specified spin-c Thom module over \(C_0(\nu_i)\widehat\otimes C_k\), and let \(F_\nu\) be its normalized Clifford multiplier. Its left coefficients are pulled back from \(L\). Tensoring on the left by \(\Gamma(i^*E)\) gives the module of sections of \(\pi^*i^*E\otimes\mathscr H_\nu\), with operator \(1_E\otimes F_\nu\). Tensoring the tube realization on the right by \(\Gamma_0(E)\widehat\otimes C_k\) gives the tube-supported module of sections of \(\tau^*E\otimes\mathscr H_\nu\), with that identical normal multiplier. In both cases the module is extended by zero from \(U\), and its range is the essential submodule for \(C_0(U)\).

These are the actual Kasparov products. Multiplication/creation by a bundle section commutes with the normal Clifford multiplier, since the bundle is even and the multiplier acts on the other factor. The creation connections are therefore exact. For the right product the positivity test is the nonnegative localized square \(2F_\nu^2\); for the left zero-operator product it is zero. The localized compact defects are the Thom defects tensored with a finite bundle on a compact patch. A finite partition on the coefficient support and norm approximation prove their compactness on the whole module. The product criterion of Section0 thus gives these operators on the completed tensor modules. Essential open extension uses Lemma0.10, without an orthogonal-complement premise.

The pointwise map \[ e\otimes\psi(v)\longmapsto T_{x,v}e\otimes\psi(v),\qquad x=\pi(v), \tag{197} \] is an even isometry preserving both coefficient actions and the normal multiplier. Its inverse is pointwise \(T_{x,v}^{-1}\). It sends the dense compact section cores onto one another; support is retained because both maps cover the identity of \(\nu_i\), and their norm is one. Hence it extends to an onto unitary of the whole completed essential modules. All spin-c/Morita factors are untouched. This unitary proves the displayed equality. Neither a characteristic-character comparison nor a proper pullback along \(\pi\) was used. \(\square\)

The ordinary-target étale bundle identity

Lemma 6.0q. If \(g:S\to Y\) is a smooth local diffeomorphism between Hausdorff second-countable manifolds and \(E\to Y\) is a smooth Hermitian bundle, then \[ u_S(g^*E)\,g_!=g_!\,u_Y(E) \quad\text{in }KK(C_0(S),C_0(Y)). \tag{198} \] The map need not be proper or injective.

Proof. The identity groupoid on \(Y\) is the zero-dimensional foliation groupoid. Lemma6.0n gives the completed module \(\mathcal E_g\) from its compact source core, with \[ \langle\xi,\eta\rangle(y) =\sum_{s\in g^{-1}(y)}\overline{\xi(s)}\eta(s), \qquad (\xi a)(s)=\xi(s)a(g(s)). \tag{199} \] It retains all the preimages. Its compact left action is local: an injective \(g\)-chart gives the rank-one identity for a supported source coefficient, and a finite partition gives the general compact-support coefficient. This is also the leaf-dimension-zero case of the complete proof of Lemma6.0n.

The right-hand product completes compact sections of \(g^*E\) in the counting inner product. On elementary tensors its map to that completion is \(\xi\otimes e\mapsto[s\mapsto\xi(s)e(g(s))]\). Its inner product is exactly the tensor inner product, as follows by summing in a fibre \(g^{-1}(y)\). Its image is dense: on a compact source chart support, choose a finite orthonormal-frame cover of its compact target image and compact target cutoffs equal to one on the smaller images. A source partition writes a section as a finite sum of source scalar coefficients times these pulled-back target sections. The tensor map therefore extends to an onto isometry.

The left-hand product has the same dense section core. The pointwise tensor map from \(\Gamma_0(g^*E)\otimes_{C_0(S)}\mathcal E_g\) has the same inner product and is onto by a source cutoff equal to one on any compact section support. Both coefficient actions match, and both operators are zero. Compact source coefficients are still compact on these modules, by the finite local frame and rank-one proof just given. These zero operators satisfy the connection and positivity conditions and hence represent the two products. The two onto tensor maps identify them as actual cycles. There is no unsupported pullback homomorphism \(C_0(Y)\to C_0(S)\) when \(g\) is nonproper: its right action is the bounded multiplier \(a\circ g\) on the counting module. \(\square\)

Identifying the ordinary map inside the full foliation construction

Lemma 6.0r. Let \(h:L\to Y\) be smooth, with \(L,Y\) compact and with a specified full stable orientation on \(h^*TY-TL\), represented in the doubled-tangent convention of (13). Regard \(Y\) as the leaf space of its zero-dimensional foliation. The full foliation product of Theorem6.0o is exactly the ordinary graph product \[ h_!=\operatorname{contract}_{k\to p}(I_!) A_n^{C(Y)\widehat\otimes C_p}, \qquad I=(h,j),\quad k=n-\dim L+\dim Y=p+2t. \tag{200} \] Here \(j:L\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^n\) is an even embedding of sufficiently large dimension, and the graph normal has the orientation of Lemma6.0j/Corollary6.0k.

Proof. The identity groupoid has no nonunit arrows. Choose the microbundle to be an open graph neighbourhood \(H\subset L\times Y\), with projection to \(L\), section \(x\mapsto(x,h(x))\), and foliation given by constant \(Y\)-coordinate. Its normal quotient is \(h^*TY\): in coordinates the quotient sends \((u,w)\) to \(w-dh(u)\). This is precisely the germ of Lemma6.0l, since its local transverse germs are the ordinary coordinate transitions of \(Y\), and its arrows are units. Theorem6.0o permits this choice of neighbourhood model.

On a uniform normal disk for \(j\), put \(N\subset p^*\nu_j\), with coordinates \((x,y,\eta)\), and \(g(x,y,\eta)=(y,j(x)+\eta)\). The map \(\Phi_j(x,\eta)=j(x)+\eta\) is an injective local diffeomorphism on that disk. Consequently \(g\) is injective: its Euclidean coordinate determines \((x,\eta)\), and its other coordinate determines \(y\). It is a local diffeomorphism, so an open embedding into \(Y\times\mathbb R^n\). The principal-space module for this open inclusion is exactly the essential module \(C_0(N)\) over \(C_0(Y\times\mathbb R^n)\), through extension by zero: the counting fibres have at most one point, and the core inner product is that zero extension. Thus \(g_!=[e_g]\).

The compact section \(k:L\to N\) has \(gk=I\). Its ordered normal \(\nu_j\oplus h^*TY\) maps to the graph normal by the quotient isomorphism of Corollary6.0k. This is exactly the normal identification induced by \(dg\). The specified orientation transported through it agrees with the graph structure constructed in Lemma6.0j; the same \(TL\oplus h^*TY\), Euclidean complement and cancellation recovery maps are used. A normalized tube for \(k\), composed with \(g\), is a normalized tube for \(I\) after that normal identification and metric transport. Hence the explicit Thom/open-extension construction gives \(k_![e_g]=I_!\). Lemma6.0e makes this equality independent of the chosen tubes. Contracting the retained Clifford block and applying the fixed Euclidean inverse proves the assertion. All line twists are retained in the same module, rather than reconstructed from their determinant. \(\square\)

The full projection formula in both K degrees

Theorem 6.0s. With the hypotheses and orientations of Lemma6.0r, for every smooth complex bundle \(E\to Y\), \[ u_L(h^*E)\,h_!=h_!\,u_Y(E)^{[p]} \quad\text{in }KK(C(L),C(Y)\widehat\otimes C_p). \tag{201} \] Consequently the ordinary wrong-way map on either K degree satisfies \(h_!(h^*[E]\,b)=[E]h_!(b)\), for every \(b\in K^*(L)\). The same statement holds for every class of \(K^0(Y)\), by differences of bundles. This is the projection formula used for sphere modification and the ordinary boundary inclusion in Theorem 6.1. Theorem 6.0w proves their composition law, and Theorem 6.0ad below proves the sphere fibre normalization.

Proof. Let \(E_n=\mathrm{pr}_Y^*E\to Y\times\mathbb R^n\). Apply Lemma6.0p to the graph embedding \(I=(h,j)\): \(u_L(h^*E)I_!=I_!u_{Y\times\mathbb R^n}(E_n)^{[k]}\). The normal orientation is the specified one in Lemma6.0r. The fixed finite contraction acts only on Clifford factors; because \(E\) is even, its tensor reassociation commutes with that contraction, including the retained odd transport of Proposition6.0i.

The Euclidean inverse is a coefficient extension of one fixed inverse, and the bundle is constant in that Euclidean direction. More precisely, \(u_{Y\times\mathbb R^n}(E_n)=u_Y(E)\boxtimes1_{C_0(\mathbb R^n)}\). On the completed module this is the tensor unitary \(e(y)\otimes a(v)\mapsto a(v)e(y)\); elementary compact sections are dense, by a finite parameter partition on compact product supports. Exterior product naturality and its associating unitary in Section0 therefore give \[ u_{Y\times\mathbb R^n}(E_n)^{[p]} A_n^{C(Y)\widehat\otimes C_p} = A_n^{C(Y)\widehat\otimes C_p}u_Y(E)^{[p]}. \tag{202} \] One can also read that map on the Euclidean inverse module: it transports the even \(E_y\) factor past the fixed oscillator/Clifford factor. Both coefficient actions and the oscillator are preserved, since the latter acts only in the Euclidean variable. There is no graded sign from \(E\). Associativity, graph projection and Lemma6.0r now prove the stated KK equality.

Apply a scalar K-class \(b\) on the left. Associativity identifies its product with \(u_L(h^*E)\) with multiplication by \(h^*[E]\); the exact scalar \(K=KK\) and bundle-class identifications of Section0 and the linked programme K-theory proofs establish this in both degrees. The right product with \(u_Y(E)\) is multiplication by \([E]\). Exterior extension of the one retained Clifford block gives the same calculation for odd \(b\). This proves the K-theory formula without a trace or rationalization.

For completeness, smooth bundles cover all coefficient \(K^0(Y)\) classes. The exact projection classification writes any class as a difference of continuous matrix projections. Approximate a continuous Hermitian projection \(P\) uniformly by a smooth Hermitian matrix \(a\) with \(\|a-P\|<1/4\). This approximation follows directly on compact \(Y\): a finite relatively compact chart cover, a smooth partition, and convolution with normalized compact smooth Euclidean bumps approximate each continuous entry uniformly by uniform continuity; symmetrization keeps the matrix Hermitian. Every spectrum of \(a_t=(1-t)P+ta\) lies within \(1/4\) of \(\{0,1\}\), by the resolvent Neumann estimate for a self-adjoint perturbation. The contour projection \(P_t=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{|z-1|=1/2}(z-a_t)^{-1}\,dz\) is therefore norm continuous in \(t\), begins at \(P\), and ends at a smooth orthogonal projection. Its final range is a smooth Hermitian bundle, and the homotopy preserves the K-class. Linearity thus proves the formula for every virtual coefficient class. \(\square\)

Composition with its induced stable orientation

The middle ordinary manifold is compact, but its Euclidean product is not. We therefore first prove the variable-radius tube comparison on a noncompact base. The resulting ordered embedding product and completed étale correspondence then give the full foliation composition law. The classical Thom/open-extension construction is also treated by [Carey–Wang, Sections4.1/4.3]; the actual KK modules, both parity contractions and full orientation recovery are proved below.

Variable-radius tubes and noncompact embedding composition

Lemma 6.0t. The normalized-tube independence and ordered embedding composition of Lemma6.0e/Theorem6.0f hold for arbitrary smooth Hausdorff second-countable source and intermediate manifolds, using their \(C_0\) algebras, specified normal spin-c modules, and whole normalized tubes. No proper base pullback is assumed. In particular they apply to a compact graph embedding into \(M\times\mathbb R^r\), followed by the product embedding \(k\times1_{\mathbb R^r}\).

Proof: variable compression. Let \(E\to X\) be the specified metric normal bundle. For any smooth positive function \(a:X\to(0,\infty)\), put \[ D_aE=\{|v|<a(x)\},\qquad q_{a,s}(x,v)=\left(x,\frac{v}{\sqrt{1+s^2|v|^2/a(x)^2}}\right), \quad 0\leq s\leq1. \tag{203} \] At zero this is the identity; at one it is a diffeomorphism onto \(D_aE\), with identity vertical differential at the zero section. For positive \(s\) its image is \(D_{a/s}E\), and its inverse has the denominator \(\sqrt{1-s^2|w|^2/a(x)^2}\). Therefore the joint parameter map is an injective local diffeomorphism onto a relatively open image. Extension by zero gives homomorphisms on \(C_0(E)\), retaining the constant Clifford algebra.

They form one norm-continuous interval homomorphism. For a compact source support \(K\subset E\), its joint image under \((s,v)\mapsto(s,q_{a,s}(v))\) is compact and lies inside the open image. The inverse formula proves continuity there. At the image boundary a nonzero level \(\epsilon\) would have preimage in the compact set \(\{|f|\geq\epsilon\}\), whose joint image is closed and remains inside that open image. Thus the extension is continuous there with value zero. Uniform continuity on a compact neighbourhood of the support, followed by density and the contractive homomorphism bound, proves norm continuity for every \(f\in C_0(E)\). No lower bound for \(a\) on all of \(X\) is needed. The global Thom equivalence gives \[ \beta_{D_aE}[e_{D_aE\hookrightarrow E}]=\beta_E, \qquad \beta_{D_aE}=\beta_E[e_{q_{a,1}}]. \tag{204} \] Both Thom classes are invertible by the global theorem and the disk algebra isomorphism, so the indicated disk inclusion has the same actual cancellation as in Lemma6.0e.

Proof: one global comparison homotopy. Given two normalized tubes, their comparison germ is \(g=\tau_1^{-1}\tau_0\). The maps \(g_s=\lambda_{1/s}g\lambda_s\), with \(g_0=1\), have the smooth extension proved in (153). Their zero-section derivative has blocks \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}I&sA_x\\0&I\end{smallmatrix}\right)\). For each \(x\), compactness of the parameter interval gives a base neighbourhood \(O_x\) and a positive radius on which every \(g_s\) is defined, locally invertible and has output vector norm less than one. Choose a countable locally finite refinement and a smooth partition subordinate to these neighbourhoods. On each refined chart choose a smaller admissible constant radius \(a_i<1/2\), and set \(a(x)=\sum_i\theta_i(x)a_i\). At a point, each active radius is admissible there, and the weighted average is no greater than their largest admissible radius. Hence every \(g_s\) is defined and locally invertible on \(D_aE\), with image in \(D_1E\). This is the full positive-minorant construction, rather than a uniform radius assertion on a noncompact base.

Each positive-parameter \(g_s\) is injective as a composition of injective maps; \(g_0\) is the identity. The joint map is therefore an injective local diffeomorphism of the relative interval domain. The same compact-support and compact-level-set proof just given gives one homomorphism \(C_0(D_aE)\widehat\otimes C_k\to C(I,C_0(D_1E)\widehat\otimes C_k)\). Its endpoints are the inclusion and the comparison map. Multiply by \(\beta_{D_aE}\), use the variable disk cancellation, and extend into the ambient manifold as in (154). This proves global tube independence directly by a single interval cycle; local equality on each compact set is not being mistaken for a global KK proof.

Proof: the actual embedding product. Write \(i:X\hookrightarrow Y\), \(j:Y\hookrightarrow Z\), \(E=\nu_i\), \(F=\nu_j\), with normal ranks \(k,\ell\). Fix whole normalized tubes \(\tau:E\to Y\), \(\sigma:F\to Z\). A spin-c connection on \(F\) gives full smooth transport \(T_{x,v}\) along \(t\mapsto\tau(x,tv)\). Every finite parameter has a compact path interval, so the exact DG-FND transport proof applies without global compactness of \(Y\). As in (157), \(\Psi(x,v,w)=(\tau(x,v),T_{x,v}w)\) is a diffeomorphism \(E\oplus i^*F\to F|_{\tau(E)}\), and \(\sigma\Psi\) is a whole tube for \(ji\), with the ordered normal splitting from its derivative.

The global \(F\)-Thom cycle restricted to \(C_0(\tau(E))\) has precisely its essential section module over \(F|_{\tau(E)}\). Compactly supported local section approximations and an ideal approximate identity prove both inclusions of that range. Its multiplier, compact defects and creation connections restrict exactly, as in (158). Transport through the actual diffeomorphism \(\Psi\) gives the coefficient Thom cycle \(\gamma\) for \(i^*F\) over the old total space \(E\), and \([e_\tau]\beta_F^{[k]}=\gamma[e_\Psi][e_{F|_{\tau(E)}\hookrightarrow F}]\). Here the only total-space transport is a homeomorphism and hence proper between the two displayed total spaces. There is no assumed \(C_0\) pullback along \(i\) or a bundle projection.

The ordered global bundle product (147)–(148) gives \(\beta_E\gamma=\beta_{E\oplus i^*F}\). Its proof uses compact old creation sections and base cutoffs. On their compact base supports the connection estimates are uniform, and at joint fibre infinity they decay; density proves the complete connection condition. Its positivity is the nonnegative expression (147). Thus it applies to this noncompact base in its proved generality. Both full spin-c transition modules tensor in order, with even transition units. Associativity and open extension now give \[ i_!j_!^{[k]}= \beta_{E\oplus i^*F}[e_{\sigma\Psi}]=(ji)_! \quad\text{in }KK(C_0(X),C_0(Z)\widehat\otimes C_{k+\ell}). \tag{205} \] The superscript retains the old \(C_k\) before the new \(C_\ell\).

Finally, the triangular splitting maps \((v,w)\mapsto(v+sAw,w)\) and their inverses are uniformly bounded on every compact base set, even though no global bound is claimed. Compact input supports consequently have uniformly compact transported supports. Their total-space algebra maps form a norm-continuous interval family by continuity and density. Transporting the metric and specified orientation gives the identical multiplier/defect homotopy on each compact coefficient support, and hence the full cycle. Connections and metrics have their previously proved interval comparisons. The variable-radius tube argument finishes their comparison. This proves the same auxiliary-choice assertion as Theorem6.0f in the stated larger generality. \(\square\)

Any compatible étale realization has the canonical germ

Lemma 6.0u. Let \(L\) be compact, \(J:L\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^N\) an even Euclidean embedding, and \(f:L\to V/F\) a smooth actual arrow cocycle. Suppose \(k:L\hookrightarrow Z\) is an embedding into a Hausdorff second-countable manifold and \(g:Z\to V/F\times\mathbb R^N\) is étale, with \(gk=(f,J)\) as an arrow-cocycle map. After shrinking near the compact section, this factorization is equivalent to the canonical factorization of Lemmas6.0l–m by a germ diffeomorphism and an actual target-arrow equivalence. If its full normal orientation is the transported specified canonical normal module, its full KK product is the canonical product, before and after the fixed Clifford contraction and Euclidean inverse.

Proof. The Euclidean coordinate of \(g\) is a single smooth map \(z:Z\to\mathbb R^N\), because every transition arrow retains that coordinate. A Euclidean tube \(\Phi_J(x,\eta)=J(x)+\eta\) is an open embedding near the compact zero section. Restrict \(Z\) to \(z^{-1}(\operatorname{im}\Phi_J)\) and define \((x(n),\eta(n))=\Phi_J^{-1}(z(n))\). These are smooth, and on \(k(L)\) are \((x,0)\).

Choose finitely many target foliation boxes and local cocycle lifts near that section. Replace each lift by its fixed plaque cross-section using its short plaque arrow, as in Lemma6.0l. At the section the given equality of cocycles supplies equivalence arrows to the fixed lifts of \(f\). Their path charts give fixed transverse holonomy branches near each centre; compose the local transverse coordinate with the inverse of that branch. This aligns it with the transverse coordinate of \(f\) at the centre. Where two aligned charts overlap, their transition branch and the canonical branch have the same germ at that centre, including the actual holonomy arrow. The finite closed-overlap shrinking proof of Lemma6.0l applies to these comparisons: branch agreement and arrow agreement are open, and compactness of the centre overlaps gives one common neighbourhood on which they agree.

The resulting local maps \(n\mapsto(x(n),y_a(n),\eta(n))\) therefore glue into the canonical neighbourhood \(N_J\). They also glue the actual arrow equivalence of the two target cocycles. They send \(k(x)\) to \(k_J(x)\). Their derivative is invertible: the étale coordinates of \(g\) are \((y_a,z)\), and replacing \(z\) by \((x,\eta)\) uses the Euclidean tube inverse. Thus this is a local diffeomorphism near the entire section.

It is injective on a smaller neighbourhood. Use a tubular disk of the compact embedding \(k\). If no common smaller disk were injective, unequal pairs with normal norms tending to zero would have equal images. Their bases have convergent subsequences in \(L\). The equal image limits force those two base limits to coincide, since the map is identity on the section. Local invertibility at that common limit contradicts equality of the late pairs. Consequently the map is a diffeomorphism of open neighbourhoods of the two sections.

Its normal derivative is the actual normal quotient isomorphism. Transport the specified normal module and metric through it. Composing a normalized tube with the diffeomorphism and using tube independence identifies the embedding factors; the total-space linear normal isomorphism is a homeomorphism and hence proper. Lemma6.0n's explicit arrow-equivalence unitary identifies the middle modules. Its essential restriction identity and the compact-source small-tube identity allow both products to use these smaller neighbourhoods. The fixed finite contractions and inverse then preserve their equality. \(\square\)

The induced stable orientation is a full module

Let \(h:L\to M\) be smooth with \(L,M\) compact, and let \(f:M\to V/F\). Put \(l=\dim L\), \(m=\dim M\), \(T=h^*f^*\tau\). Prescribe the stable orientations of \(h\) and \(f\). Choose even Euclidean embeddings \(u:L\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^r\), \(j:M\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^n\), with positive graph normal ranks. The actual normal modules of Lemma6.0j are \[ E_h=\nu_u\oplus h^*TM,\quad k_h=r-l+m, \qquad E_f=\nu_j\oplus f^*\tau,\quad k_f=n-m+q. \tag{206} \] The graph \(I_h=(h,u)\) is an embedding into \(M\times\mathbb R^r\). Follow it by \(k_j\times1\) into \(N_j\times\mathbb R^r\). The composite \(K=(k_jh,u)\) has ordered normal \(E=E_h\oplus h^*E_f\), through the normal exact-sequence splitting of Lemma6.0t. Its full module is \(\mathscr M_E=\mathscr M_{E_h}\widehat\otimes h^*\mathscr M_{E_f}\), with right block \(C_{k_h}\widehat\otimes C_{k_f}=C_k\), \(k=n+r-l+q\). The two Euclidean blocks are even.

Lemma 6.0v. This ordered normal module induces precisely a stable orientation of \((fh)^*\tau-TL\), the sum of \(h^*TM-TL\) and \(h^*(f^*\tau-TM)\). It can be converted to the doubled-tangent convention by explicit finite Morita cancellation, and Lemma6.0j recovers the entire normal module from it. Its class is independent of \(u,j\) and the exact-sequence splitting. A line twist \(H\) of \(h\) and a line twist \(D\) of \(f\) give the composite twist \(H\otimes h^*D\), not merely its squared determinant.

Proof: the normal quotient. The étale map \(g_j\times1\) has Euclidean component \((j(x)+\eta,w)\). Its composite with \(K\) is \((fh,J)\), where \(J=(jh,u):L\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^{n+r}\) is an embedding because \(u\) already is one. The transverse derivative identifies the normal quotient of \(K\) with \((T\oplus\mathbb R^{n+r})/d(fh,J)(TL)\). The transverse differential \(d^\perp(fh):TL\to T\) is global: in each fixed holonomy branch the derivative of the local transverse lift changes by exactly the derivative transition of \(T\).

Writing \(U=TL\) with a metric and \(G_J=dJ^*dJ\), the explicit quotient isomorphism to \(E_J=\nu_J\oplus T\) sends \[ [(t,z)]\longmapsto(\eta,t-d^\perp(fh)v), \qquad v=G_J^{-1}dJ^*z,\quad \eta=z-dJv. \tag{207} \] Adding \((d^\perp(fh)a,dJa)\) changes \(v\) to \(v+a\) and leaves both output components fixed. Its inverse sends \((\eta,t)\) to \([(t,\eta)]\), so it is a smooth quotient isomorphism. Compose it with the ordered normal splitting to obtain \(\chi:E\to E_J\). Transport the metric and full module through \(\chi\). This supplies the specified positive-rank spin-c normal structure in Lemma6.0u.

The stable normal identity is an identity of actual ordered bundle representatives: \[ (E_h-\underline{\mathbb R^r})+ (h^*E_f-\underline{\mathbb R^n}) =E-\underline{\mathbb R^{n+r}} \simeq T-U. \tag{208} \] The swap of the two even Euclidean blocks uses their canonical complex exterior unitary. Their stable orientation is the ordered tensor of the full normal modules followed by that same Euclidean cancellation. This defines the induced orientation of the sum in (13), with its transition phases; the equality is not inferred from characteristic classes.

Proof: exact double-convention recovery. Let \(Q_U=U\oplus U\) have the canonical interleaved complex module \(\mathscr M_{Q_U}\). Before using \(\rho_J\), compare the metric transported by \(\chi\) with the orthogonal sum metric on \(\nu_J\oplus T\) by Corollary6.0d's positive metric isometry. This transports the full module, including its line, rather than treating a nonorthogonal map as a Clifford *-map. Let \(L_c=U\oplus T\), and use Lemma6.0j's explicit isometry \(\rho_J:E_J\oplus Q_U\to L_c\oplus\mathbb R^{n+r}\). Carry \(\mathscr M_{E_J}\widehat\otimes\mathscr M_{Q_U}\) through \(\rho_J\) to a module \(P:A_{L_c}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}\rightsquigarrow C_{l+q}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}\). On its right this uses the consecutive-generator regrouping \(C_k\widehat\otimes C_{2l}=C_{k+2l}=C_{l+q+n+r}=C_{l+q}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}\); no generator permutation is made by this regrouping. Write \(S=\Lambda^*\mathbb C^{(n+r)/2}\), with the fixed interleaved Clifford action. Define \[ \mathscr M_{L_c}= (A_{L_c}\widehat\otimes S^*) \widehat\otimes_{A_{L_c}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}}P \widehat\otimes_{C_{l+q}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}} (C_{l+q}\widehat\otimes S). \tag{209} \] Both finite evaluation maps of Lemma0.12 give the exact recovery \(\mathscr M_{L_c}\widehat\otimes C_{n+r}\cong P\), because the canonical even Euclidean module \(S\widehat\otimes S^*\) is the right regular Clifford unit through its actual matrix-unit evaluation. Pulling this recovery through \(\rho_J\) and cancelling \(\mathscr M_{Q_U}\) by the two recovery maps of Lemma6.0j returns exactly \(\mathscr M_{E_J}\). Thus the canonical graph construction with this induced stable orientation has the original full product normal module.

When \(l+q>0\), the local even/odd Clifford reconstruction in Lemma6.0j gives the principal spin-c interpretation of \(\mathscr M_{L_c}\). When \(l+q=0\), the cancellation can give a graded line, including an odd line. Its grading is part of the stable orientation. The canonical rank-zero unit is still the even trivial line; an odd line is not declared to be that unit. Use a positive even stabilized normal representative, as above, to interpret such rank-zero stable data. Accordingly the doubled-tangent phrasing after (13) is understood after even stabilization when necessary. Lemma6.0j's actual finite construction (177)–(178) also applies directly to this graded line: the only principal reconstruction it needs is for the positive normal rank \(k\). The original stable virtual-bundle convention is retained, including its orientation sign.

Proof: independence and twists. Interpolate two choices of \(u\) by the common even cos/sin embedding family, and do the same for \(j\). Lemmas6.0g–j give the actual normal families of \(I_h\) and \(k_j\); their product normal exact sequence, the displayed \(\chi\), \(\rho_J\) and both finite cancellations vary smoothly. On a common Euclidean stabilization they therefore give a full \(\mathscr M_{L_c}\) family over \(I\times L\), with fixed left Clifford bundle and fixed right algebra. Parameter transport can be chosen to preserve these actions. In positive rank, choose a spin-c connection whose projected orthogonal connection is the fixed product connection: from any connection subtract the equivariant lift of the difference of its orthogonal projection and that product connection, using \(\mathfrak{spin}^c=\mathfrak{so}\oplus i\mathbb R\). Its interval transport has fixed orthogonal frame and hence intertwines the Clifford action. In rank zero use the unitary connection of the graded line, with its locally constant grading retained. The exact DG-FND transport proof gives even endpoint module isomorphisms. Under a further even Euclidean stabilization the added canonical modules cancel by the same finite evaluations and exterior wedge unitary. Thus the induced stable orientation is independent of these choices.

Splittings have the explicit triangular interpolation of Lemma6.0t, so give the same full comparison family. If the two original orientations are twisted by \(H,D\), their normal modules are tensored by those lines, by (180). The product normal module is therefore tensored by \(H\otimes h^*D\). The displayed cancellations move only Clifford/spinor factors, so return that same line, including any torsion and its grading. This proves all assertions. \(\square\)

Composition of the actual foliation products

For parity \(a,b\in\{0,1\}\), write \(x\# y\) for the ordered graded KK product retaining \(C_a\) before \(C_b\), followed by the fixed contraction to \(C_{a+b\bmod2}\). If both are odd, this is the actual \(C_1\widehat\otimes C_1=C_2\) matrix Morita evaluation on \(\Lambda^*\mathbb C\). Moving a retained odd factor past preceding even pairs uses the even triple-cycle unitaries of Proposition6.0i. This is the convention already used in Section0; all products below can equivalently retain the full normal Clifford blocks until the final contraction.

Theorem 6.0w. With the hypotheses and the induced full stable orientation of Lemma6.0v, \[ h_!\# f_!=(f\circ h)_! \quad\text{in }KK(C(L),A\widehat\otimes C_p), \qquad p=q-l\pmod2. \tag{210} \] This is an actual KK equality for the completed foliation correspondence. It applies in particular to the sphere projection and the boundary inclusion needed for geometric-cycle descent, with their induced stable orientations.

Proof. Use the factorization of \(f\) by \(k_j\), \(g_j\), the Euclidean inverse \(A_n\), and the ordinary graph factorization of \(h\) by \(I_h=(h,u)\), \(A_r\). The latter is exactly the full zero-foliation construction by Lemma6.0r. Lemma6.0t identifies the product embedding class of \(I_h\) and \(k_j\times1_{\mathbb R^r}\) with the class of \(K=(k_jh,u)\), carrying precisely the ordered normal module of Lemma6.0v. It applies despite the noncompact intermediate \(M\times\mathbb R^r\).

The middle module of the product foliation is the onto isometry \(\mathcal E_{g_j\times1}\cong\mathcal E_{g_j}\widehat\otimes C_0(\mathbb R^r)\) proved in Theorem6.0o. It preserves the two actions, every counting lift and the zero operator. For its principal space this is exactly \(P_{g_j}\times\mathbb R^r\), not a numerical fibre identification. Thus \((g_j\times1)_!=(g_j)_!\boxtimes1_{C_0(\mathbb R^r)}\).

Exterior product naturality in Section0 moves the even coefficient inverse \(A_r\) successively through \(k_j\) and \(g_j\). Its associating unitary retains the old normal block before the new normal block. All creation/positivity requirements of these products are already proved for the embedding, the actual zero-operator correspondence, and the ordered Bott classes. Therefore, retaining the full normal blocks until the stated contraction, the product is \[ \begin{aligned} h_!\# f_! &=\operatorname{contract}_{k\to p} \bigl((I_h)_!(k_j\times1)_!^{[k_h]} (g_j\times1)_!^{[k]}\bigr) A_r^{D_n\widehat\otimes C_p}A_n^{A\widehat\otimes C_p}\\ &=\operatorname{contract}_{k\to p} \bigl(K_!(g_j\times1)_!^{[k]}\bigr) A_{n+r}^{A\widehat\otimes C_p}, \qquad D_n=A\otimes C_0(\mathbb R^n). \end{aligned} \tag{211} \] The Euclidean target is ordered \(\mathbb R^n\) then \(\mathbb R^r\); its inverse first removes the new \(r\) block and then the old \(n\) block. That is exactly the inverse composition (148), with its fixed even wedge unitary. The two inverse identities, rather than equality of an integer index, identify it with the fixed \(A_{n+r}\).

For clarity, late and early Clifford contraction give the same displayed product through actual maps. Tensor reassociation combines the two ordered full normal algebras as \(C_{k_h+k_f}\). Their canonical matrix factors contract by \(\xi\otimes\eta^*\mapsto\theta_{\xi,\eta}\) and \(\xi^*\otimes\eta\mapsto\langle\xi,\eta\rangle\). The exterior wedge isometry identifies consecutive even pairs. For a retained odd factor, the fixed even three-generator cycles move it past such pairs and preserve the normalized odd central volume, as proved in Proposition6.0i. If two odd factors remain, their ordered \(C_2\) evaluation is the specified final matrix contraction. Composing these associating/evaluation isometries identifies the early contracted tensor module with the late contracted one, preserving both actions and gradings. No ungraded odd permutation is used and no scalar sign is dropped.

Finally, \(g_j\times1\) is étale and its composite with \(K\) is \((fh,J)\), with \(J=(jh,u)\) an even embedding. Lemma6.0v proves that its full normal module is the canonical one for the induced stable orientation. Lemma6.0u therefore identifies this actual factorization product with the canonical \((fh)_!\), through a germ diffeomorphism, a completed arrow-equivalence unitary and essential restriction. The last display proves the claimed equality. \(\square\)

Figure 6.0d. Lemmas6.0p–v, Theorems6.0s/6.0w, equations (196)–(211), Exercises44–45. The first panel gives the actual norm-one coefficient transport on the entire normalized tube, including the exact cylinder phase. The second panel retains the product embedding order and every holonomy lift in the completed étale module. The third panel gives the normal quotient, positive metric comparison, full finite-module recovery and ordered inverse cancellation. All Clifford/module tensors are graded, and \(\#\) includes the stated parity contraction. The last panel is the exact point-to-circle-to-point example with the prescribed normal frames; it distinguishes the two stable orientation gradings of virtual rank zero. These are diagrams of maps and modules. The classical Thom/open-extension method is treated by [Carey–Wang, Section4]; all displayed KK and grading comparisons are proved above.
