Boundaries, sphere bundles and geometric cycles

The two geometric relations require more than a fibrewise index. A boundary needs its entire map cocycle, bundle and spin-c structure to extend to a double. A sphere bundle needs a global clutch bundle and the inverse full orientation, including any line twist. We prove these constructions in that order.

The geometric prerequisites are Lemma 3.1 and the tubular construction in Manifold duality, the diagonal and Wu classes, and Sections 1–4 of Connections and parallel transport. Theorem 2.1 and Section 3 of Topological K-theory of spaces, pairs and vector bundles provide the full relative bundle comparison and disc compactification. The KK and Clifford inputs are the complete preceding arguments of Sections 0 and 6.

These geometric relations and a zero-section charge construction are also treated by [Liu, Section 2]. The full foliation correspondence, double and ordered orientation comparisons used here are proved below.

Embeddings and the graph construction

Lemma 6.0x. Let \(i:M\hookrightarrow Y\) be a smooth embedding of manifolds without boundary, with \(M\) compact. Give its normal quotient \(E\) a specified full stable spin-c orientation, allowing the canonical even zero-rank module. Give \(i\) the resulting stable orientation of \(i^*TY-TM\). Its ordinary graph wrong-way class is the actual tubular class \[ i_!=\beta_E[e_\tau]\in KK^{\operatorname{rank}E}(C(M),C_0(Y)). \tag{216} \] In particular the canonically oriented identity map has class \(1_{C(M)}\). Any specified line twist, including the grading of a stable rank-zero line, is retained in this comparison.

Proof. Take an even Euclidean embedding \(j:M\to\mathbb R^n\), with \(n\) large enough that every normal rank used below is positive. The maps \[ I_s(x)=(i(x),s j(x)),\qquad 0\le s\le1, \tag{217} \] are embeddings on an open interval about \([0,1]\), even at zero: the first component already is an embedding. Their normal quotients form a smooth bundle on that whole interval. Fix a splitting \(i^*TY=di(TM)\oplus E\), and identify the quotient by \[ E\oplus\underline{\mathbb R^n}\longrightarrow\nu_{I_s}, \qquad(\eta,z)\longmapsto[(\eta,z)]. \tag{218} \] This is an isomorphism. To reduce \((y,z)\) to this form, uniquely write \(y=di(v)+\eta\) and subtract \((di(v),s dj(v))\); injectivity follows from the same direct-sum decomposition. The matrices and their inverses depend smoothly on \(x,s\).

Here is the full orientation check, rather than an inference from the existence of a normal bundle. Put \(W=TM\), \(T=i^*TY\), and give \(Q=W\oplus W\) its fixed interleaved complex-double module. The orientation of \(E=T-W\) determines the orientation module on \(L=W\oplus T\) by the inverse finite construction of (177)–(178). Over (218) its recovery is transported through the invertible bundle map \[ (\eta,z,u,v)\longmapsto(u,di(v)+\eta,s dj(v)+z) : (E\oplus\mathbb R^n)\oplus Q\longrightarrow L\oplus\mathbb R^n. \tag{219} \] Transport the metrics by the positive comparison of Corollary 6.0d before extending this map to a Clifford *-isomorphism. Pull back the full module \(\mathscr M_L\widehat\otimes C_n\) and apply \(\mathcal C_Q\). Both evaluation maps of (177)–(178) give a smooth full normal module family. At \(s=0\) the map is the unstabilized recovery followed by the identity on the new Euclidean block. The even block move and exterior evaluation in (179) identify its module with \(\mathscr M_E\widehat\otimes C_n\), in that order.

At \(s=1\) compare it with the specified graph construction. Use the complement \(\nu_j\oplus T\) to the graph tangent, sending \((\zeta,t)\) to \([(t,\zeta)]\). Its recovery before orthonormalization is \((\zeta,t,u,v)\mapsto(u,t+di(v),dj(v)+\zeta)\). The recovery map (176) omits \(di(v)\) in its second coordinate. These two recoveries are joined by the explicit invertible target shears \[ (u,t,z)\longmapsto (u,t+\lambda\,di((dj^*dj)^{-1}dj^*z),z), \qquad0\le\lambda\le1. \tag{220} \] They are invertible because their diagonal blocks are identities. The positive factors making \(dj\) isometric are joined to their identities inside the positive invertible cone. Changes between the two complements are affine splittings of the same quotient; their convex interpolations remain splittings. Applying the same positive metric transport, full module pullback and \(\mathcal C_Q\) to these paths gives actual smooth orientation-module paths between (219) and (176). On an interval a principal spin-c connection gives an even endpoint intertwiner, by the full associated-transport proof in the connection lesson, Sections 3–4. The underlying orthogonal connection can be prescribed to the chosen metric/splitting path: its lift is unique in the spin Lie algebra, and the central connection is retained. Thus these are precisely the prescribed full orientations. A line tensor is unaffected by every cancellation map; an odd line is not replaced by an even unit.

Lemma 6.0g applied to (217), with this full family, identifies the embedding classes of its endpoints. At zero the embedding is the composite of \(i\) and the zero section \(Y\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbb R^n\). The ordered embedding product of Lemma 6.0t, and its even stabilization comparison, identify its class with \(i_!\widehat\boxtimes\beta_n\). This remains valid when \(Y\) is noncompact: the compact source is \(M\), and the intermediate tube uses the positive variable radius of that lemma. Multiplying by the fixed Euclidean inverse \(A_n\) gives \(i_!\). At one it gives exactly the graph definition. Its full Euclidean product cancels by both inverse identities, not just by a numerical index. This proves (216). For the identity embedding the normal has rank zero, its tube is the identity, and its canonical Thom module is the even standard module with zero operator. Its class is the identity. \(\square\)

A separating hypersurface has a null Thom unitary

Lemma 6.0y. Let \(D\) be a compact smooth manifold without boundary and let \(M=\partial Q\subset D\) be the boundary of a codimension-zero compact smooth submanifold \(Q\). Orient the normal line by the outward unit normal and give it the canonical spin-c structure. For \(i:M\hookrightarrow D\), \[ (i_!)_*[1_M]=0\quad\text{in }K_1(C(D)). \tag{221} \] This is an integral statement and holds for a disconnected boundary.

Proof. Choose a collar with the normal coordinate increasing from \(Q\) to its complement, and use its whole-line normalized tube \(\tau:M\times\mathbb R_v\to D\). Its negative end approaches the inside edge of the collar and its positive end approaches the outside edge. The full canonical normal module is the right regular \(C_1\) module. The scalar Thom cycle of Corollary 6.0d is consequently \((C_0(M\times\mathbb R)\widehat\otimes C_1,1,s(v)\varepsilon)\), where \(s(v)=v/\sqrt{1+v^2}\). Theorem 0.14, including its naturality for the possibly degenerate extension-by-zero homomorphism, sends its scalar class to the explicit unitary \[ U(\tau(x,v))=\exp(\pi i(1+s(v))),\qquad U=1\quad\text{off the collar}. \tag{222} \] The difference from identity tends to zero at both collar ends, so this is exactly the extended compact-unitary class. Lemma 6.0x identifies it with the ordinary map construction, with the same normal orientation.

The real function \(\Theta:D\to[0,2\pi]\) is defined as follows. It is zero on the part of \(Q\) beyond the inside collar edge, equals \(\pi(1+s(v))\) on the collar, and is \(2\pi\) on the outside part. Its one-sided limits are respectively zero and \(2\pi\), hence it is continuous across both edges. It is defined independently on all components, including components disjoint from \(M\). The formula \[ U_t(x)=\exp(i t\Theta(x)),\qquad0\le t\le1, \tag{223} \] is a norm-continuous path of unitaries in \(C(D)\), since \(\|U_t-U_{t'}\|\le2\pi|t-t'|\). It joins identity to \(U\). Thus its \(K_1\)-class is zero. The compactness of \(D\) matters: we are homotoping unitaries in the unital algebra \(C(D)\). We have not asserted that \(U_t-1\) vanishes at infinity in an arbitrary noncompact ambient manifold. \(\square\)

Corollary 6.0z. In Lemma 6.0y let \(g:D\to V/F\) have a specified full stable orientation and let \(E_D\) be a complex bundle on \(D\). Give \(g i\) the orientation induced in Theorem 6.0w, with the canonical outward normal first. Then \[ (g i)_!([i^*E_D])=0. \tag{224} \]

Proof. The ordinary projection formula and actual composition give \(i_!([i^*E_D])=[E_D]i_!([1_M])=0\) and \((g i)_!([i^*E_D])=i_!([i^*E_D])\widehat\otimes_{C(D)}g_!\). Here the first scalar class is odd; Theorem 6.0w includes the exact ordered Clifford contraction for this degree. Formula(221) therefore proves (224). \(\square\)

Extending all the bordism data across a double

The boundary orientation of a K-oriented map \(f:Q\to V/F\) is specified by \(f^*\tau-T(\partial Q)=(f^*\tau-TQ)|_{\partial Q}\oplus\mathbb R_{\rm out}\), with the normal line put first when taking the embedding-then-map product. The finite full-module evaluation of Lemma 6.0v fixes the block order. This defines the induced orientation, rather than choosing a new structure whose determinant only agrees with it.

Lemma 6.0aa. Let \(Q\) be a compact smooth manifold with boundary, \(f:Q\to V/F\) a smooth map cocycle with a specified stable orientation, and \(E\to Q\) a complex bundle. There exist a compact smooth double \(D\), a smooth map cocycle \(g:D\to V/F\), a complex bundle \(E_D\to D\), and a full stable orientation of \(g\), such that on \(\partial Q\) their map, bundle and induced boundary orientation are exactly those of \((Q,E,f)\). The hypersurface \(\partial Q\) separates the first copy of \(Q\) from its reflected second copy.

Proof: collar and constant data. In a finite boundary-chart cover, choose the coordinate inward vectors and multiply them by a smooth partition of unity. Their normal component is strictly inward along the boundary; every coefficient is nonnegative and their sum is one. Extend their finite sum to a smooth vector field on a neighbourhood inside \(Q\). The full local-flow proof of Lemma 3.1 in the manifold-duality lesson applies in boundary charts by extending the smooth coefficients across their coordinate hyperplanes. Compactness of the boundary gives a common positive existence time. The flow map \(c: \partial Q\times[0,\delta)\to Q\) has invertible derivative at time zero, since its time derivative is transverse. Shrink \(\delta\) so it is locally invertible everywhere on this strip. It is injective after a further shrink: if distinct pairs at times tending to zero had equal images, compactness gives a common limiting boundary point, and its local inverse contradicts the equality. A failure of all smaller radii gives precisely such a sequence. Thus it is a smooth collar with a smooth inverse onto its relative open image.

Choose a smooth \(\alpha:[0,\delta)\to[0,\delta)\) equal to zero near zero and to \(t\) for \(t\) beyond a smaller collar. It can be \(t\chi(t)\), where \(0\le\chi\le1\) is a smooth cutoff. Define \(r(c(x,t))=c(x,\alpha(t))\), and put \(r=1\) off this collar. This is smooth. The interpolation \(\alpha_u(t)=(1-u)t+u\alpha(t)\) gives a smooth map homotopy fixed on the boundary. Replacing the map cocycle by \(f r\) makes every lift and every transition arrow independent of \(t\) near zero. This is done by literal pullback of the cocycle, so all triple identities and all holonomy arrows remain. It is not merely a homotopy of its leaf images. Pullback by \(r\) similarly gives a coefficient bundle equal to the boundary bundle's product near zero, with its exact specified boundary identification.

We must also transport the orientation without using the singular derivative \(dr\). On \(L_u=TQ\oplus(f r_u)^*\tau\) over \(Q\times[0,1]\), a metric connection on \(f^*\tau\) transports the second summand along the paths \(f\circ r_u\) in their cocycle bundles; equivalently pull back the fixed bundle connection along the map \((x,u)\mapsto r_u(x)\) in \(Q\). Leave the first summand fixed. This supplies isometries from \(L_0\) to \(L_u\), with the identity on the boundary. Transport the entire prescribed orientation, including its scalar transition line, along them. Near the boundary use a product metric and the collar splitting \(L_1=\mathbb R_{\rm out}\oplus(T\partial Q\oplus f_{\partial}^*\tau)\). Principal parallel transport in the collar direction identifies its orientation bundle with its restriction at time zero. Its projected orthogonal connection is chosen to make this product frame constant; the spin connection is its lift and its central connection is retained. The lift exists because the differential of the spin cover is an isomorphism on the orthogonal Lie algebra. On this restricted principal bundle the construction uses the actual full connection, whose existence and complete-path transport are proved in the connection lesson, Theorems 3.1/4.1 and Corollary 4.2. The associated transports are even unitaries, not determinant-line identifications. No orientation is inferred from \(dr\).

The connection arguments also apply on a compact manifold with boundary: in each relative principal product chart choose the zero potential and average the local connection forms with a smooth relative partition of unity. The reproduction and equivariance identities are unchanged. Their coordinate coefficients extend across the boundary hyperplane, so the full finite-interval ODE and parameter transport proof applies there. Thus no extension of the original orientation beyond \(Q\) has been presumed at this step.

Proof: the reflected principal structure. The rank \(k=\dim Q+q\) of \(L_1\) is at least one when the boundary is nonempty. A stable orientation on this positive-rank bundle is its actual principal spin-c structure by Lemma 6.0j's reconstruction. In the positive real Clifford algebra let \(e_1^2=1\), and let \(R_0\) negate the first coordinate while fixing the others. The map \[ \kappa([s,z])=[e_1 s e_1,z] \tag{225} \] is an automorphism of \(\mathrm{Spin}^c(k)\). It preserves the central \(U(1)\) coordinate and the relation \((-s,-z)\sim(s,z)\). Its projection is \(A\mapsto R_0 A R_0\): on single Clifford vectors conjugation by \(e_1\) is \(-R_0\); the two minus signs cancel on every even Clifford product defining the spin group. The assertion also holds in rank one, where this automorphism is the identity.

If \(b_a\) are local oriented orthonormal frames of \(L_1\), with spin-c transition units \(g_{ab}\), give the same real bundle its opposite orientation using the frames \(b_a R_0\) and the full transition units \(\kappa(g_{ab})\). Their projections are precisely the transitions of those opposite frames. The cocycle identity is preserved by the automorphism, and the unchanged scalar coordinates retain every line twist. This is a specified full principal structure on the second copy, denoted \(P^{\rm opp}\).

On the collar choose frames whose first vector is the outward normal. Their transitions stabilize \(e_1\). Each such spin transition is an even product of the remaining Clifford generators, and therefore commutes with \(e_1\); hence \(\kappa(g_{ab})=g_{ab}\), including the scalar phase. For completeness, the entire preimage of the orthogonal stabilizer is \(\mathrm{Spin}^c(k-1)\): plane-rotation lifts in the complement cover its special orthogonal group, and two lifts of a fixed orthogonal matrix differ by a central phase. This follows from the kernel calculation in Lemma 6.0j. In rank one the complement is zero and its surviving line phase is retained.

Form the double by identifying both boundary copies and using the collar coordinate with opposite signs on the two sides. These collar charts and the interior charts have smooth transitions. The finite collar and interior cover proves second countability; disjoint interior points have disjoint neighbourhoods and collar charts separate boundary points, so the double is Hausdorff. It is compact as the continuous image of the two compact copies, and has no boundary. The tangent identification across the seam reflects the normal and is the identity on \(T\partial Q\). On the pullback transverse bundle it is the identity, since the map cocycle is constant in the normal coordinate. Thus it sends the opposite adapted frame on the second side to the adapted frame on the first side. The above equal full transition units let us glue \(P^{\rm opp}\) to \(P\) by the identity in these principal charts. This gives an actual smooth principal spin-c bundle over \(TD\oplus g^*\tau\), projecting to its oriented frame bundle. The complete scalar phases glue, so no square of a line has been substituted for the line itself. Metrics and principal data are product data near the seam; they extend smoothly on the interiors.

The constant map cocycles glue by the identity arrows, and the constant coefficient bundles glue by their boundary identifications. Denote them by \(g\) and \(E_D\). On the first side their restriction to the seam is the original \(f_{\partial}\), coefficient \(E|_\partial\), and full orientation. Finite double/Euclidean recovery in Lemma 6.0v commutes with restriction and with these identity gluing maps. Its composition with the canonical outward normal therefore recovers exactly the specified induced boundary orientation. This verifies the last assertion on the full module, rather than only on its underlying virtual bundle. If some components of \(Q\) have no boundary, double them disjointly; they impose no boundary assertion. \(\square\)

Theorem 6.0ab (full bordism relation). For every compact smooth K-oriented bordism \((Q,E,f)\), with the induced full boundary orientation just specified, \[ (f|_{\partial Q})_!([E|_{\partial Q}])=0 \quad\text{in }K_{q-\dim\partial Q}(A). \tag{226} \] In particular the wrong-way assignment respects the bordism relation of the geometric cycle group.

Proof. Apply Lemma 6.0aa and Corollary 6.0z to its actual double. All data on the separating hypersurface agree, so (224) is exactly (226). Neither a longitudinal analytic index nor a rational character calculation is used. Direct sums and disconnected boundaries are included by the finite coefficient-module sum.

The opposite boundary convention gives the additive inverse, with its full orientation. This can be checked explicitly. For a positive-rank normal module with principal transition \(g\), the opposite structure has transition \(\kappa(g)\) and physical Clifford coordinate \(R_0v\). Left multiplication by \(e_1\) satisfies \(e_1\kappa(g)=g e_1\) and \(e_1 c^+(R_0v)=-c^+(v)e_1\). It is right-module linear, unitary and odd. It identifies the opposite Thom cycle with the original module with reversed grading and negated operator, the additive inverse cycle of Section 0. Every intervening double and even matrix evaluation is even, so the same identification passes through full normal recovery and final parity contraction. Stabilize a zero-rank normal first if necessary; its line grading remains part of this calculation. Thus a bordism written as the incoming boundary with opposite orientation together with the outgoing boundary proves equality of their two assigned K-classes, with the integral sign and every line twist retained. \(\square\)

The actual clutch bundle

Let \(W\to M\) be a metric real bundle of positive even rank \(2a\), with its specified full spin-c structure, over a compact smooth manifold \(M\) without boundary. Let \(S_W=S_W^+\oplus S_W^-\) be its spinor bundle, with the chirality (145). Write \[ \widehat M=S(W\oplus\mathbb R_s),\qquad \pi:\widehat M\to M,\qquad n(x)=(0,1). \tag{227} \] On the closed north hemisphere take \(\pi^*S_W^+\), and on the closed south hemisphere take \(\pi^*S_W^-\). On their common equator the clutch isometry is \[ c^+(w):S_{W,x}^+\longrightarrow S_{W,x}^-, \qquad |w|=1. \tag{228} \] It is unitary because \(c^+(w)^*c^+(w)=I_+\) and \(c^+(w)c^+(w)^*=I_-\), by the full Clifford relation and \(|w|=1\). It changes spinor parity. Gluing by this specified isometry defines a complex bundle \(b_W\) on \(\widehat M\). Here the restrictions of a complex bundle on the two hemispheres are ungraded; the signs enter the difference class below. The construction is smooth: on an equatorial annulus use \(c^+(w)/|w|\) as its transition between the hemisphere trivializations. It is equivariant under the actual full spin-c transitions, so every central line twist of \(S_W\) is retained.

Give the disc bundle \(Q=B(W\oplus\mathbb R_s)\) the map \(p:Q\to M\) and the full stable orientation \(p^*TM-TQ=-p^*(W\oplus\mathbb R_s)\), using the inverse of the ordered sum orientation of \(W\) and the canonical positive real line. An inverse stable orientation means the inverse full Clifford Morita module: its two products recover the canonical cancellation module by the rank-one and inner-product evaluations of Lemma 6.0j. In the ordered inverse the last real-line block is removed first and the \(W\) block second, exactly as in (148). In particular an original twist by a line \(H\) becomes \(H^*\), rather than a trivialization of \(H^2\). Choose a horizontal splitting of the tangent sequence; its affine space of splittings and positive metric transport give the same full stable orientation. Give \(\pi=p|_{\partial Q}\) its induced boundary orientation, with the outward normal first. This specifies the orientation of \(\pi\) used below.

Lemma 6.0ac (north-section class and full orientation). With these orientations, \[ n_!\widehat\otimes_{C(\widehat M)}\pi_!=1_{C(M)}, \qquad n_!([1_M])=[b_W]-[\pi^*S_W^-]. \tag{229} \] The first equality is in KK; the second is in \(K_0(C(\widehat M))\).

Proof: the full orientation. The normal of \(n\) is exactly \(W\), and give it the specified structure. At the north section, the vertical tangent of \(Q\) is the ordered \((W,\mathbb R_s)\). The outward normal is \(+\partial_s\). Its boundary tangent is \(W\). The full inverse for the ordered \((W,\mathbb R_s)\) removes the last real-line block first. The ordered normal followed by this inverse therefore has the adjacent factors \(\mathbb R_s,-\mathbb R_s,-W\). Their actual evaluation contracts the first pair and leaves the inverse module of \(W\). If the positive-rank doubled realization places the even \(W\) block between the two line factors, use the fixed even block move of Proposition 6.0i before that evaluation; it preserves every generator action and the normalized odd volume. Both actual evaluations for the real-line factor are used; the normalized odd generator is retained until its final ordered \(C_2\) evaluation. The full positive \(W\) module of \(n\) then cancels this inverse by \(\xi\otimes\eta^*\mapsto\theta_{\xi,\eta}\) and \(\xi^*\otimes\eta\mapsto\langle\xi,\eta\rangle\). These maps are even, preserve the inner products and both actions, and are onto by their finite matrix bases. The result is the canonical even rank-zero unit, including its line and grading. This is exactly the full induced composite orientation of Lemma 6.0v, since its recovery maps are these same evaluations. The composite \(\pi n\) is the identity map. Theorem 6.0w and Lemma 6.0x therefore give the first identity in (229).

Proof: the whole clutch class. The north open hemisphere is the image of the whole-bundle tube \[ \tau(x,v)=\frac{(v,1)}{\sqrt{1+|v|^2}}. \tag{230} \] It fixes \(n\) and its normal derivative at zero is the identity. It is a diffeomorphism, with inverse \(v=w/s\) for \(s>0\). The radial disc coordinate \(v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}\) identifies this hemisphere compactification with \((B(W),S(W))\); this is the proper radial homeomorphism proved in the topological K-theory lesson, Section 3. Its boundary is the equator, with \(c^+(v)/|v|\) the specified boundary comparison.

The Thom cycle in Corollary 6.0d, after its fixed even Clifford contraction, is the pulled-back spinor module with lower block \(c^+(v):S_W^+\to S_W^-\), divided by \(\sqrt{1+|v|^2}\). Its relative K-class is the exact bundle triple \((\pi^*S_W^+,\pi^*S_W^-,c^+(w))\) on this disc pair. Here is its actual relative projection. Set \(T=c^+(v)/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}\). Both defects \(1-T^*T\) and \(1-TT^*\) are the scalar \(1/(1+|v|^2)\) on their respective spinor bundles. The even index formula of Theorem 0.14 gives, on \(\pi^*(S_W^-\oplus S_W^+)\), \[ P_T(v)=\frac1{1+|v|^2} \begin{pmatrix}|v|^2 I_-&c^+(v)\\c^+(v)^*&I_+\end{pmatrix}, \qquad P_0=\begin{pmatrix}I_-&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}. \] One verifies \(P_T^2=P_T=P_T^*\) by \(c^+(v)c^+(v)^*=|v|^2 I_-\). The difference \(P_T-P_0\) vanishes at fibre infinity, uniformly over compact \(M\). Its range is the image of the isometry \[ S_{W,x}^+\longrightarrow S_{W,x}^-\oplus S_{W,x}^+,\qquad \xi\longmapsto\frac{(c^+(v)\xi,\xi)}{\sqrt{1+|v|^2}}. \] At the equator that frame has limit \((c^+(w)\xi,0)\); the range projection tends to \(P_0\), independently of the direction \(w\). Extend it by \(P_0\) over the south hemisphere. It is a continuous projection there, whose range bundle is exactly the clutch bundle with comparison (228). Its reference range is \(\pi^*S_W^-\).

For precision about nontrivial base bundles, \(P_0\) need not be a constant scalar matrix. Choose finite Hermitian embeddings of the two bundles over the compact base and apply the complementary rotation of the topological K-theory lesson, Theorem 2.1, formula (2.7), to their projections. That rotation turns a pair agreeing on the boundary into a pair with the common constant reference of that formula. It therefore computes a class in the external relative ideal, rather than incorrectly placing the varying bundle projection in its unitization. Stabilizing the Fredholm cycle of Theorem 0.14 by these same finite complements gives that same relative index: its doubled unitary has first-column range \(P_T\), and its reference is the target bundle projection. The full relative excision identification in the topological K-theory lesson, Theorem 2.1 thus sends it to the specified disc triple. The projection-range construction above identifies the forgetful class with \([b_W]-[\pi^*S_W^-]\), with the kernel-minus-cokernel sign of Theorem 0.14. For one complex coordinate, swapping the two displayed blocks gives the positive projection with range \((1,z)\) and reference \((0,1)\), as computed in its Theorem 3.1. No inference from one fibre or a rational character is needed for a nontrivial \(W\).

The pair \((\widehat M,\{s\le0\})\) has the same open relative ideal. The bundle pair \((b_W,\pi^*S_W^-)\), with the identity comparison on the south hemisphere, restricts on the north disc to exactly this triple: on the equator that comparison is (228). the topological K-theory lesson, Theorem 2.1 and relative excision identify its relative class with the zero-extension of the Thom class. Its forgetful map is \([b_W]-[\pi^*S_W^-]\). Lemma 6.0x identifies the zero-extended tubular class with the ordinary map \(n_!\). This proves the second identity in (229). \(\square\)

Theorem 6.0ad (sphere fibre normalization). For this full specified orientation of \(\pi\), \[ \pi_!([1_{\widehat M}])=0, \qquad \pi_!([b_W])=[1_M]\quad\text{in }K_0(C(M)). \tag{231} \] For every complex-bundle difference \(a\in K^0(M)\), \[ \pi_!(\pi^*a\,[b_W])=a. \tag{232} \] These equalities include nontrivial and two-torsion line twists in the chosen spin-c structure.

Proof. The first identity in (231) is Theorem 6.0ab for the disc bordism \((Q,\mathbf1,p)\), with exactly its induced boundary orientation. The disc has compact base and fibre, so is compact and its boundary is precisely \(\widehat M\). The preceding full bordism proof applies even though \(p\) itself is a map from a manifold with boundary; it only uses the closed double's actual wrong-way class. No unproved class for \(p\) is used.

Apply \(\pi_!\) to the second identity in (229). The first identity in (229) sends its north-section term to \([1_M]\). The ordinary projection formula of Theorem 6.0s sends \([\pi^*S_W^-]\) to \([S_W^-]\,\pi_!([1_{\widehat M}])=0\). This proves the second identity in (231). Apply the same projection formula to \(a\), using additivity for bundle differences, to obtain (232). The spin-c line tensor in \(b_W\) and its dual tensor in the orientation of \(\pi\) have been carried through the actual evaluations in (229). There is no torsion loss. \(\square\)

The zero-rank case

If \(W\) has rank zero with the canonical even unit orientation, \(\widehat M=M_+\sqcup M_-\). Define \(b_0\) to be the trivial line on \(M_+\) and the zero bundle on \(M_-\). Its rank can be different on distinct connected components. The bordism is \(Q=M\times[-1,1]\), with its vertical line positive toward the \(+\) end. The induced stable rank-zero orientation of the projection is the even unit on \(M_+\) and the odd unit on \(M_-\). Indeed the two outward normals are \(+\partial_s\) and \(-\partial_s\), and the reflection calculation in Theorem 6.0ab negates the latter class before the ordered odd–odd contraction. Consequently the actual coefficient modules give \[ \pi_!(a_+,a_-)=a_+-a_-,\qquad \pi_!([b_0])=[1_M],\qquad\pi_!(1,1)=0. \tag{233} \] These are exact module calculations with zero operators. If the even stable zero-rank orientation has an additional line \(H\), use \(b_0=(H,0)\); the projection's full modules are \(H^*\) and \(\Pi H^*\). They give \(H^*a_+-H^*a_-\), and the same normalization follows from \(H\otimes H^*\cong\mathbf1\). This makes explicit why both zero-rank components cannot silently be assigned the same even orientation. It also agrees with (229): \(S_W^-=0\) and the north section has its specified even line.

The geometric relation descends

Theorem 6.0ae (geometric-cycle descent). For the smooth compact map-cocycle model and full stable orientations of Section 5, the assignment \[ (M,E,f)\longmapsto f_!([E]) \quad\text{in }K_{\dim M-q}(A) \tag{234} \] respects all three geometric relations. It therefore defines a homomorphism \(K_{*,\tau}^{\mathrm{geom}}(BG)\to K_*(A)\) for this specified model.

Proof. Direct sum and disjoint union are the direct sums of the actual finite bundle and correspondence modules; Section 0 proves their product additivity. Theorem 6.0ab proves the entire oriented bordism relation, including the opposite sign and full line twist.

For a sphere modification give \(f\pi\) the induced orientation from \(\pi\) above followed by the original full orientation of \(f\). Both sphere and base are compact. Theorem 6.0w applies and (232), or (233) in rank zero, gives \[ (f\pi)_!([\pi^*E\otimes b_W]) =\pi_!([\pi^*E\otimes b_W]) \widehat\otimes_{C(M)}f_! =f_!([E]). \tag{235} \] The added vertical rank is even, so it changes neither the cycle parity nor the retained final odd Clifford factor. Its full orientation is the composed one, whose normal evaluations were checked in (229); it is not a new determinant-only choice. The three relations thus generate equal images, proving descent. This statement does not identify the geometric group with another topological model, prove twisted analytic/geometric duality, or prove the longitudinal analytic index theorem. Those are distinct subsequent theorems. \(\square\)

Figure 6.0e. Lemmas 6.0x–z, 6.0aa and 6.0ac; Theorems 6.0ab, 6.0ad and 6.0ae; equations (216)–(235); Exercises 46–47. The phase curve samples \(v\in[-4,4]\); its dashed lines are the exact limits zero and \(2\pi\). The global bounded phase gives the norm-continuous null-homotopy (223). The second panel reflects the first normal coordinate and glues the full principal spin-c transitions, including the central phase. The last panel gives the whole north/south clutch bundle, ordered inverse cancellation, disc-bordism normalization and the signed rank-zero calculation. These are diagrams of maps and modules. The classical geometric relations are treated by Connes and by Liu; all displayed foliation KK and full orientation assertions are proved here.

Full-size descent PNG · Editable descent SVG.

Theorem 6.1 (assembly from wrong-way maps). For the compact smooth map-cocycle model of Section 5, use the inverse Bott class of Corollary 0.20 and the full vector-bundle Thom class in (16), with the specified stable orientation. Then

\[ \mu[(M,E,f)]=[E]\otimes_{C(M)}f_! \tag{17} \]

defines a homomorphism \(K_{*,\tau}^{\mathrm{geom}}(BG)\to K_*(A)\).

Proof. Theorem 6.0o proves invariance under the full factorization choices, cocycle refinements and smooth orientation-preserving homotopies. Theorem 6.0ae proves direct-sum, bordism and sphere-modification descent. Its bordism proof extends all principal and cocycle data across a smooth double and contracts the separating normal-line unitary. Its sphere proof identifies the entire clutch bundle and both ordered orientation cancellations, then proves the coefficient normalization. Thus (17) is independent of every defining cycle relation. Additivity of the actual bundle and correspondence modules makes it a homomorphism. \(\square\)

This gives geometric-cycle descent in the stated smooth cocycle model. Theorem 6.2 below constructs the full twisted cohomology class and proves its compact-test duality. Theorems 7.25 and 7.29 prove the full longitudinal comparison and its symbol action in both degrees. The identification with other assembly models and the isomorphism assertions for assembly have their separate scope in the following sections.

An analytic K-homology class \(x\in KK^j(A,\mathbb C)\) gives the numerical homomorphism below. Theorem 6.2 identifies it with the compact tests of one full twisted cohomology class:

\[ [(M,E,f)]\longmapsto \mu[(M,E,f)]\otimes_A x\in K_{j+\dim M-q}(\mathbb C). \tag{18} \]

Theorem 6.1 and associativity show that it respects all the relations. Theorem 6.2 supplies the full geometric twisted cohomology class on \(BG\), with all integral classes and normal-line data retained, and proves that (18) is its oriented compact-test pairing.

The full twisted cocycle on the classifying space

The remark on native page 35 of [Connes, §11] concerns twisted cohomology \(K^{*,\tau}(BG)\). We specify its full group and construct the analytic class, then identify its oriented compact tests with (18). The topology and operator-field arguments below use actual holonomy arrows throughout. The classical methods are treated in [Connes–Skandalis, §§3–4], Moerdijk, §§1–5, and Emerson–Meyer, §3.2. All proofs needed here, including the classifying replacement, both manifold triangles and the extension convention, are supplied below.

Theorem 6.2 (analytic K-homology gives a full twisted geometric cocycle). Let \(G=\operatorname{Hol}(V,F)\), \(A=C_r^*(G)\), and \(\tau=TV/F\). There is a locally compact Hausdorff second-countable CW model \(X\) for the weak homotopy type of \(BG\), carrying the pullback of its universal actual cocycle and entire normal bundle \(E_X\). With the negative graded-opposite Clifford and positive right-\(C_1\) conventions below, set

\[ K^{j,\tau}(BG)=RKK_X^j(C_0(X,\operatorname{Cl}^+(E_X)^{\rm op}),C_0(X)), \qquad K_j^{\rm an}(A)=KK^j(A,\mathbb C). \tag{382} \]

The analytic group has the complete stable semisplit extension-theory interpretation proved in E. There is a natural homomorphism \(\chi:K_j^{\rm an}(A)\to K^{j,\tau}(BG)\), independent of the complete model with its specified normal comparison. For every compact smooth actual cocycle \(f:M\to V/F\), its full pullback is the field class \(\chi_f\). Every prescribed full stable orientation on \(TM\oplus f^*\tau\) and Hermitian test bundle gives precisely the integral numerical pairing (18), in both degrees, through the full KK equality in (465)–(466). The construction retains all torsion and classes invisible on individual compact stages.

Proof. Parts T and C construct the entire analytic family and identify its full Clifford–Fredholm group. B, R, A, U, M, W, V and Q supply the actual classifying cocycle and locally compact model; D supplies its full group and the single analytic class. G proves both actual manifold triangles; H and I give the complete orientation and graph-normal comparison. E proves the source extension convention in both degrees. These are the following complete arguments. The letters label proof parts; equations have the lesson's consecutive numbering.

T1. The actual parameter tube and its étale correspondence

Let M be a compact smooth manifold, f a smooth actual G-arrow cocycle from M to V/F, E=f*τ and q=rank E. No orientation of E or TM is imposed. The full microbundle construction of Lemma6.0l gives p:H_f→M, its section ι, normal E and actual arrows over a neighbourhood of ι. In its original charts the plaques have constant transverse coordinate; p need not be constant on a plaque. Choose a fibre-preserving normalized tube as in Theorem6.0o. It is the new target parameter in(383) that is fixed along the target leaves. A positive radial compression identifies all of E with an open smaller neighbourhood U of ι in H_f. Denote the resulting map by ρ:E→U. It keeps pρ=π_E and has positive scalar normal derivative at zero. The arrow cocycle g on U has local transverse maps g_a and exactly the prescribed f_a on the section, up to its specified short-arrow equivalence.

Use the foliation on V×M with tangent F×{0}. Its groupoid is G×M and its reduced algebra is C(M,A), A=C*r(G). Define the local lifts

\[ \widehat g_a(y,v)=(g_a(\rho(y,v)),y), \qquad \widehat g_{ba}(y,v)=(g_{ba}(\rho(y,v)),y). \tag{383} \]

These are actual arrows, including all holonomy lifts. In transverse coordinates the derivative has the block form [[D_v g_a,D_y g_a],[0,1]]. The first diagonal block is invertible after the tube shrink. The source E has dimension dimM+q, exactly the transverse dimension of this target. Thus (383) is an étale cocycle from the unit foliation of E. Lemma6.0n gives the entire countably generated Hilbert C(M,A)-module L_f and a compact, nondegenerate coefficient action φ_f:C0(E)→K(L_f), with cycle operator0.

The module is C(M)-linear: on its principal-space core, multiplication by h(π_E(z)) on the left equals multiplication by h(y) on the right, because the target source parameter is precisely y. Convolution retains y and its inner product is a continuous A-valued function of y. The equality holds on the completion by the essential multiplier action. The compact-action proof is the actual short-arrow normalized rank-one proof of Lemma6.0n; it is not pointwise ordinary compactness on a holonomy cover.

T2. The full finite Clifford cancellation, without a spin-c choice

Write C_M=C(M), C_E=C(M,Cl+(E)), P_E=C(M,Cl+(E)^op), where the opposite is the graded opposite. For a homogeneous b, its product and involution are b^op·c^op=(-1)^{|b||c|}(cb)^op and (b^op)*=(-1)^{|b|}(b*)^op. These conventions make graded right multiplication an adjoint-preserving representation.

Let W_E be the finite Hermitian bundle Cl+(E), graded by word parity, with scalar-part trace inner product. Its antisymmetrization identifies it orthogonally and equivariantly with ΛE_C. On an orthonormal frame, write L_i for left multiplication by the positive generator and R_i for graded right multiplication: R_i(w)=(-1)^{|w|}we_i. Their actual actions are

\[ L_i=e_i+\iota_i,\qquad R_i=e_i-\iota_i, \qquad e_i=(L_i+R_i)/2,\quad\iota_i=(L_i-R_i)/2. \tag{384} \]

Here e_i means exterior multiplication, consistently with(129), and is distinct from its self-adjoint a_i=e_i+ι_i. Formula(384) follows on every ordered word: if i is absent, L_i and R_i have the same insertion sign; if i is present, their removal signs are opposite. In particular R_i is skew-adjoint with square−1, as required by the graded-opposite involution. Left and graded-right actions graded commute. Exterior multiplication and contraction generate every matrix unit: the vacuum projection is ∏_i(1−e_iι_i), and creation words, that projection and adjoint creation words give the matrix units between all exterior monomials. The resulting faithful representation is

\[ C_E\widehat\otimes_{C_M}P_E \cong C(M,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}W_E). \tag{385} \]

All actions are orthogonally equivariant; no frame, determinant line or orientation was chosen globally. Both finite Morita evaluations are ξ⊗barη↦θ_{ξ,η} and barξ⊗η↦<ξ,η>. Their inner products give isometries, and the full matrix units and local finite frames give onto ranges. Finite partitions prove fullness over C(M). Their zero-operator cycles satisfy both product criteria by the complete imprimitivity proof0.12. Rank zero gives W_E=C_M and both identities literally.

T3. A twisted Bott cycle with its two actual inverse products

Put A_E=C0(E,π*Cl+(E)). The complete raw b_E,d_E of Lemma6.0a/Theorem6.0c are C(M)-linear and have both inverse products. Their full proofs use orthogonal transitions only, so their balanced external products with P_E keep that linearity. Let m_E be the pullback to E of the even Morita equivalence (385). Define

\[ \widetilde b_E=(b_E\widehat\otimes_{C_M}1_{P_E})m_E \in KK_{C_M}(P_E,C_0(E)),\qquad \widetilde d_E=m_E^{-1}(d_E\widehat\otimes_{C_M}1_{P_E}). \tag{386} \]

The target of the balanced raw product is A_E⊗_{C_M}P_E, identified with the compact endomorphisms of π*W_E. Both actual Morita evaluations and the two global identities(136), before any parity reduction, give tilde b_E tilde d_E=1_{P_E} and tilde d_E tilde b_E=1_{C0(E)}. The source has the graded-opposite Clifford action, the target has its ordinary function action, and no odd blocks are silently interchanged.

Its concrete representative is Γ0(E,π*W_E), right C0(E), with the source acting by the graded right Clifford operators R_b, and bounded phase L_{c+(v)}/sqrt(1+|v|²). Formula(384) makes its graded source commutators zero; its square defect is the scalar−1/(1+|v|²). The pullback endomorphism Morita module identifies this with (386). This also fixes the rank-one sign in the full Clifford convention; no separately ordered real Bott pair is being identified here.

T4. The actual universal transverse test family

Define

\[ k_f=\widetilde b_E\cdot[\mathcal L_f,\phi_f,0] \in KK_{C_M}(P_E,C(M,A)). \tag{387} \]

A product representative is π*W_E⊗_{C0(E)}L_f with the same bounded Clifford phase in v. Local finite W_E frames and compact fibre cutoffs express a creation vector as a finite column of C0(E) coefficients. Each acts compactly on L_f. Therefore its complete creation map is rectangular module compact. Norm approximation by these sections treats every creation vector. Multiplication by the bounded phase preserves compactness and adjoints give the second error against the zero operator. The first positivity anticommutator is exactly2B²≥0. Its localized square defect is the compact φ_f(1/(1+|v|²)), in finite W_E corners; graded source commutators vanish. This verifies the actual product criterion, including the nonunital C0(E) action, rather than just naming a KK product.

For x∈KK^j(A,C), its external C(M)-coefficient cycle is C(M)-linear. The complete product theorem0.6 therefore gives

\[ \chi_f(x)=k_f\cdot\tau_{C_M}(x) \in KK^j_{C_M}(P_E,C_M). \tag{388} \]

Every adjointable operator in its final module is automatically C(M)-linear, since the specified central left parameter action equals the strict right multiplier action. Thus the actual product construction does not discard parameter linearity. This is a full Clifford-twisted family class, not the scalar index obtained by integrating over M. Additivity, homotopy and all torsion are retained by the full KK products.

T5. Compact smooth pullbacks and choices

For h:N→M with N compact smooth, E_N=h*E and the pulled cocycle define the same construction over C(N,A). Use the pulled metric and tube. The whole principal space of its étale cocycle is exactly the pullback of the principal space in(383) along the target parameter h. On compact chart cores, the map from the balanced coefficient pullback of L_f sends ξ⊗a to h*ξ·a. Its A-valued inner products are the original ones evaluated at h(y), with the same convolution arrow and counting multiplicities. It is an isometry in the complete C(N,A)-module norm. Finite parameter charts and separated parameter/arrow tests give dense range: compact core functions on the pullback are uniformly approximated by finite sums of functions of N times pullbacks of local arrow-chart functions, then the common Schur bound makes that a module-norm approximation. Completion is onto. This proves actual coefficient base change, not merely equality of individual parameter fibres.

The Clifford regular module, both finite evaluations and (386) pull back by their literal formulas. The map of total bundles is proper for compact M,N, so the proved proper-pullback naturality of Corollary6.0d applies. Associativity and the exact even parameter transport0.13 now give χ_{fh}(x)=h*χ_f(x), with the identified Clifford twist. No degree sign comes from the even parameter pullback.

Changing arrow cocycle representatives uses the actual principal-space unitary of Lemma6.0n. Its normal derivative transports E and its Clifford actions; choose the transported metric first, then the positive metric homotopy of Corollary6.0d. Refinements use the identical glued principal space. Tube/compression changes use the fibre-preserving interpolation and shrink/expansion homotopy of Theorem6.0o. These are entire parameter modules with compact actions before endpoint evaluation. They give homotopies of(387) and(388), retaining all opposite-Clifford coefficients. The rank-zero construction uses the zero normal tube and even unit of (385); a test-manifold tangent orientation has never been introduced.

C1. The continuous-base hypothesis and the exact algebras

Let X be locally compact, Hausdorff and second countable. Let f be a continuous actual G-arrow cocycle on X. Its arrows have their Lie-groupoid topology, including every holonomy branch; a relation between leaf images is not a cocycle. Set E=f*τ, C_X=C0(X), P_X=C0(X,Cl+(E)^op), A=C*r(G). The bundle E is continuous and has a continuous metric. All Clifford tensor products are graded. A C_X-linear cycle has its central left C_X action equal to the right essential multiplier action. Write

\[ KK_X(P_X,C_X)=KK_{C_X}(P_X,C_X). \tag{389} \]

Both coefficient algebras are separable. A continuous section of a finite-dimensional bundle over this X is approximated using countably many precompact charts, continuous base functions and finite fibre coefficients. The same applies to C0(E) and C0(X,A). These are ordinary separable C*-algebras, so the proved product theorem0.6 applies. No product theorem for a non-locally-compact BG or a pro-C*-algebra is being asserted here.

All assertions C2–C5 also apply to X×K for compact finite polyhedra K, including a simplex and any union of its faces. They apply to continuous base maps; no derivative of a base map is used.

C2. Locally finite germs and a fibrewise smooth normal neighbourhood

Choose a countable locally finite shrinking V_a with compact closures inside cocycle charts U_a. This can be obtained from a precompact countable basis and a subordinate locally finite partition: enlarge the closed supports slightly inside their assigned U_a. Local finiteness may be retained by taking the enlargements inside a previously locally finite refinement. A compact closure meets only finitely many of the enlarged sets. Thus every closed double or triple overlap used with a fixed chart has only finitely many partners.

On each chart replace f_a by a fixed plaque cross-section using its short plaque arrow. Conjugate transition arrows exactly as in(181). On a neighbourhood of any base point of a closed double overlap, the resulting arrow lies in one transverse path chart. Its restriction to the two plaque cross-sections is a fixed smooth transverse branch. Its dependence on the base enters only through the continuous centre h_a(x). Cover that compact double overlap by finitely many such branch neighbourhoods. The equality of germs on their closed overlaps gives an open neighbourhood of each centre on which both transverse maps and actual arrows agree. This is an open arrow-chart intersection, not a selection of an arrow from its endpoints alone. A finite subcover makes the agreement uniform on a smaller neighbourhood of each compact overlap. Treat inverse, diagonal and triple identities the same way.

For any x, only finitely many of these closed-overlap conditions are active on a small neighbourhood of x. Their finite common transverse radius is positive there. Choose a positive continuous radius δ(x) below all those local bounds. Here is an explicit minorant construction: choose a locally finite base cover on whose members a constant positive lower bound r_j works, take a subordinate partition λ_j, and replace r_j by r_j/2. Then δ=Σ_j λ_j r_j/2 is positive and is below the admissible bound at each point, since every active r_j is admissible there. Further local bounds for the images of compositions can be included before making this choice.

The centred fibre changes are continuous in x and smooth in v, with all vertical derivatives continuous:

\[ F_{ba}(x,v)=H_{ba}^{x}(h_a(x)+v)-h_b(x),\qquad F_{ca}(x,v)=F_{cb}(x,F_{ba}(x,v)). \tag{390} \]

The second identity is used whenever its intermediate vector remains inside the chosen chart disk. Inverses and identities have that same domain convention. Glue D_a={(x,v):x∈V_a, |v|<δ(x)} by the direct pair relation w=F_ba(x,v), requiring both vectors to be in their chart disks. This relation is already transitive by(390), so chains add no new identifications. On each D_a×D_b it is closed: equality of base points is closed and the pair map is defined on the entire relevant input disk. The components of the disjoint union are open and closed; hence the whole relation is closed. Its quotient is open because partial fibre changes are homeomorphisms on open domains. Closedness plus openness separate inequivalent classes by the product-neighbourhood argument of Lemma6.0l. The quotient H_f is therefore Hausdorff and second countable. It is locally a product of an open subset of X and a fibre disk, and is locally compact. Its projection p and section ι are continuous, and its vertical normal is the derivative cocycle E.

There is no assertion that H_f is a manifold or that X is smooth. There is also no assertion that its plaques keep p fixed. The original transverse coordinates give the germ data, while p is used for the independent target parameter.

Construct a fibre-preserving normalized tube from E to H_f. For completeness, local fibre charts carry the spray \(\dot z=v, \dot v=0\). A change of fibre chart has vertical acceleration D_z²h(v,v). Patch these sprays using a locally finite partition continuous in x and smooth in the fibre, obtained from product base functions and fibre bump functions. The patched spray has continuous vertical derivatives, base velocity v and acceleration of order |v|² at zero. The usual contraction argument for its integral equation is uniform on a precompact parameter/chart set: a vertical-derivative bound makes its Picard map a contraction for a short time. Iterating finitely many such times near a fixed zero trajectory gives time one, continuous dependence on x and smooth dependence on v. Its derivative at zero is the identity on the vertical normal. The parameter inverse theorem uses this same uniform derivative bound; its contraction proof gives a continuous fibre inverse near zero. Local fibre injectivity needs only a sufficiently small disk at each x. Since p is fixed, points over different x can never have the same image. A further positive continuous minorant chooses one variable-radius disk on which the whole map is an open fibre embedding.

Positive radial compression then gives a normalized map ρ:E→U⊂H_f defined on the entire E. Explicitly, compression into radius r(x) uses v↦v/sqrt(1+|v|²/r(x)²); its vertical derivative at zero is one. This formula is continuous in x, fibre smooth, and has its continuous fibre-smooth inverse on that open disk. All extended arrows are defined on U after one further variable-radius shrink if needed.

C3. The completed whole module, not separate fibre completions

Use the target G×X, with reduced coefficient algebra C0(X,A). The relative cocycle on E is (g_a(ρ(x,v)),x), with the extended actual arrows and the same x. In any transverse path chart its vertical derivative D_vg_a is invertible. Thus its principal space has relative source-anchor charts over X: locally the anchor to X×V is a homeomorphism, smooth in the manifold variables. There is no derivative in x in this assertion. The source-anchor fibres at (x,y) are discrete and countable, with every distinct holonomy lift retained.

Complete the chart core using the counting/convolution formulas(186). Inner products are elements of C0(X,A). To verify this norm topology, first consider finitely many chart kernels with compact parameter and arrow support. In a relative product chart, their coefficients vary continuously in x. A finite parameter partition approximates them uniformly by separated parameter/arrow kernels. Uniform row and column bounds on this compact support, from the same Schur estimate used in Lemma6.0n, turn that into convergence in reduced norm. Coefficients vanish outside their compact parameter projection. General compact core sections are finite sums of these charts. The regular-fibre identity(187) proves matrix positivity in the faithful direct sum over (x,y); it supplies the C0(X,A) norm, rather than an independently chosen fibre norm. The quotient and completion give L_f.

The algebra identification C*r(G×X)=C0(X,A) has the same verification: separated kernels have exactly the sup_{x,y} regular norm, finite partitions give every compact chart kernel, and compact-support continuous A-valued functions are uniformly approximated by such separated arrow-core values. Their closures agree isometrically.

For c∈C0(E), multiplication c(b(z)) is adjointable and contractive on L_f by the regular-fibre maps. A source coefficient supported in one injective relative transverse chart is a normalized short-plaque rank-one map. The plaque half-density can be chosen continuously in x, with a strictly positive continuous normalizing integral on its compact support. The calculation in Lemma6.0n therefore remains an actual equality of module operators. A finite partition on a compact source support proves compactness for every compact-support c; sup-norm density proves

\[ \phi_f:C_0(E)\longrightarrow\mathcal K(\mathcal L_f). \tag{391} \]

Countable chart exhaustions and countable coefficient approximations give a norm-dense core, using these same Schur bounds. Its right span, with a countable approximate identity of the separable coefficient algebra, proves countable generation. The action is nondegenerate because source cutoffs converge on the compact chart core. Multiplying by h(π_E(z)) on the left equals the right parameter multiplier h(x) on every core vector and hence on the completion. This proves its exact C_X linearity. The zero operator is a genuine C_X-linear C0(E),C0(X,A) cycle with compact left action.

The raw Clifford cycles6.0a–c also extend to this continuous base. Their domain arguments differentiate only in the vector fibre. The compact-frequency bounds, oscillator eigenbundles, rotations, translations and positive metric identifications are continuous in base charts and orthogonally equivariant. Compact base cutoffs make their localized resolvents compact with exactly the existing uniform estimates(132),(135),(138)–(142). Fibre smoothing gives a dense coefficient algebra; no base smoothing is required. Their actual inverse homotopies retain both Gaussian evaluations. Therefore(385)– (387), with C0(X) in place of C(M), give a whole class

\[ k_f\in KK_X(P_X,C_0(X,A)),\qquad \chi_f(\eta)=k_f\,\tau_{C_X}(\eta)\in KK_X^j(P_X,C_X), \quad \eta\in KK^j(A,\mathbb C). \tag{392} \]

The concrete first product still has the finite exterior bundle and phase L_{c+(v)}/sqrt(1+|v|²). Compact-support creation sections are rectangular compact maps because of(391); their norm approximations treat every creation section. Its positive anticommutator is2B² and its localized defect is(391) applied to the source coefficient divided by1+|v|². For the final product, the single separable coefficient algebra C0(X,A) and the single tensor module are used in theorem0.6. Every adjointable operator on this module is C_X-linear, by the exact central multiplier equality. This constructs its operator before taking any parameter fibre.

C4. The exact Clifford average and geometric field model

For compact X, P_X is unital. Compress a C_X-linear cycle to the even projection φ(1); the complement has zero representation and is degenerate. The compressing difference is compact. Normalize its odd operator to a self-adjoint contraction as in Section0. Thus its square defect is globally compact. Let R_i be the representation of the negative generators of P_X on a local orthonormal chart, and set R_I=R_{i_1}⋯R_{i_k} in increasing order, R_empty=1. They are homogeneous unitaries. Define the finite operator average

\[ \mathfrak a_E(F)=2^{-q}\sum_{I\subset\{1,\ldots,q\}} (-1)^{|I|}R_I F R_I^*. \tag{393} \]

Each summand is an odd self-adjoint contraction. The maps T↦−R_iTR_i* on odd T are commuting involutions: R_i²=−1, and R_iR_j=−R_jR_i has a central scalar sign which cancels in conjugation. Consequently(393) is their product of averaging projections. Its fixed operators are exactly those graded-commuting with every R_i. In particular it is idempotent, contractive and fixes F if F already graded-commutes with the source Clifford action.

It is independent of frame. Under an orthogonal frame change, the degree-k ordered words change by the real orthogonal exterior-power matrix. In the sum of R_I F R_I* for that degree, its two occurrences cancel by orthogonality. The factor(−1)^k is constant on that degree. Thus the averages glue over E without a spin-c or orientation choice. For an already compressed representation, each F−(−1)^|I|R_IFR_I* is compact on a chart after multiplication by a base cutoff: it is the graded commutator with R_I followed by its unitary adjoint. Choose a finite partition on X with supports inside orthonormal charts and extend the cut-off words as genuine P_X coefficients. Their source commutators are compact by the Kasparov condition. Summing proves F−a_E(F)∈K(H). The straight line between them is a Kasparov homotopy; its square and source-commutator defects remain compact. The new operator has exact graded Clifford commutation.

The noncompact essential-source reduction is also explicit. Let (H,φ,F) be any C_X-linear P_X,C_X cycle. On a relatively compact open set V choose u∈C_c(X) equal to one on V and regard u1_Cl as an actual P_X section. At x∈V the operator p_x=φ(u1_Cl)_x is an even projection, since u²−u vanishes on V. It does not depend on u: for h supported in the common region where two choices equal one, C_X linearity gives hφ((u−v)1_Cl)=φ(h(u−v)1_Cl)=0. These locally defined operators therefore give a bounded *-strong projection field p. They define a genuine adjointable projection on H, rather than merely a pointwise support projection. Indeed pξ is locally the section φ(u1_Cl)ξ, is bounded in fibre norm by ||ξ_x||, and vanishes at infinity. A locally finite partition and compact cutoffs approximate it by actual module sections. Its adjoint is itself. The fibre norm is faithful, so p²=p on H.

The source action satisfies pφ(a)=φ(a)p=φ(a). Moreover pH is exactly its essential submodule. On a compact support, finitely many local units express pξ as a finite sum of φ(u_j1_Cl)h_jξ; compact cutoffs approximate a general pξ. Thus pH is the closed source span and is complemented, with countable generation inherited from the adjointable projection on the countably generated H. The complementary source action is zero. For h∈C_c(X), a finite partition subordinate to local-unit regions gives h[F,p]=Σ_j h h_j[F,φ(u_j1_Cl)]∈K(H): F commutes exactly with the right central base multipliers. Hence replacing F by pFp+(1−p)F(1−p) changes it by a locally compact operator. The straight line preserves every localized cycle condition. The zero-source summand is degenerate and can be discarded. This proves the essential-source reduction on every such X; it does not assume that an essential submodule of an arbitrary Hilbert- module representation is complemented. The finite, locally unital bundle source and exact C_X linearity are what prove it here.

On pH, the same average proof is localized by h∈C_c(X), with finitely many orthonormal charts on its support. The average is a global bounded adjointable operator. Its difference from F and its square defects are compact after each base cutoff. Approximation in C0(X) proves all localized Kasparov conditions. For the particular cycle(392), the source is already nondegenerate: a scalar Clifford approximate identity acts as the right base multiplier and converges on every tensor vector, even when the chosen A representation of η is degenerate.

A geometric Clifford–Fredholm field over X means: a countably generated graded continuous Hilbert field, a nondegenerate continuous P_X action with its exact base action, and an odd self-adjoint contraction F graded-commuting with the fibre Clifford action. Its localized defect is a norm-continuous compact field, vanishing at infinity after multiplication by every C0(X) coefficient. Isomorphisms, addition of degenerate fields and homotopies use the same whole fields over X×I. Odd degree retains the ordered positive right C1 coefficient from Section0; it is never replaced by a trace.

Here is the operator topology, with its proof. Stabilize a whole countably generated C0(X) module by0.2 as a projection p on a graded standard module. The vectors p(x)e_n are continuous multiplier sections; multiplying them by a compact base cutoff gives actual module sections. The projection p(x) is *-strongly continuous. An adjointable F gives a bounded *-strong field pFp. Every compact module map gives a norm-continuous compact field: rank-one fields have this property, and norm limits preserve it. Conversely a norm-continuous compact field T=pTp which vanishes at infinity is a compact module map. Its image over a compact parameter support is a compact subset of the ordinary compact operators. Standard finite-coordinate projections P_N approximate that subset uniformly. Thus pP_NTP_Np converges in norm to T and is a finite matrix of these multiplier vectors, with continuous coefficients vanishing at infinity. Each coefficient factors into two continuous square-root factors vanishing at infinity (using its polar factor away from its zeros), so these are actual compact rank-one maps of module sections. Alternatively apply the compact base cutoff first, making every p e_n in the finite sum an actual section. Cutting off the parameter first treats a general T. This proves both directions. Multiplication by a bounded *-strong unitary preserves this compact norm topology: approximate a compact operator by finitely many rank-one vectors, use strong continuity on those vectors, and bound the residual by twice its norm. Hence the topology is independent of the chosen stabilization; it is not an arbitrarily chosen operator-norm topology on all Fredholm operators.

That paragraph writes the even degree. In odd degree the right coefficient is C0(X)⊗C1 with its ordered positive generator. The fields are Hilbert C1-module fields, and stabilization uses the standard C1 module. Its finite-coordinate corners have C1 entries. A faithful finite-dimensional regular representation of C1 gives their exact operator norm and realizes their compact ideal as K(ℓ²)⊗C1. The same finite-coordinate approximations, multiplier vectors, compact cutoffs and square-root factorization apply with those entries. The local-unit projection and average are adjointable right-C1-linear operators and never remove that coefficient. Thus the odd assertion below follows by the identical whole-module proof with this finite coefficient, rather than by forgetting an odd block or taking its scalar trace.

For every X under C1, forgetting exact Clifford commutation identifies the group of these fields with KK_X^j(P_X,C_X). Surjectivity uses the local-unit projection, normalization and(393) on the whole module. Injectivity follows by performing them on the whole KK homotopy over X×I, including its continuous representation. Its left C0(X×I,Cl E^op) action is obtained by finite interval partitions and compact base cutoffs from the original P_X action and the right interval multipliers; contractivity follows in the faithful fibre representation, so it extends in sup norm. The local-unit projection restricts to each endpoint's essential projection. Intrinsic averages restrict to endpoint averages, and fix operators which already graded-commute. Thus the forgetful homotopy becomes an exact Clifford–Fredholm homotopy with the same endpoint classes. Zero-source summands, degenerate fields, unitary maps and sums have the same description. No exhaustion or inverse-limit assertion occurs here. This identifies the full twisted field group on X, including torsion and classes invisible on every compact stage, with this RKK group. Parts Q and D below identify the complete model and its exact normal twist.

C5. Base change and finite coherent choices

Let h:Y→X be any continuous map between locally compact Hausdorff second-countable bases. A nonproper h has a nondegenerate map C0(X)→M(C0(Y)), u↦u∘h; it need not map into C0(Y). Nondegeneracy follows because h sends every compact subset of Y into a compact subset of X, where a C0(X) approximate identity converges uniformly. For a C_X coefficient algebra B, use the balanced base-changed algebra B_Y=C0(Y)⊗_{C_X}B. In the cases at hand these are precisely C0(Y,A), C0(h*E), the pulled Clifford section algebra, and C0(Y). The dense map g⊗b↦g(y)b(h(y)) is isometric in the faithful fibre norm. Local bundle charts and a finite partition on a compact support give dense range. Thus these are algebra identifications, not nonproper C0 pullback homomorphisms. The original B acts nondegenerately by multipliers of B_Y, so a module H_B has its well-defined tensor pullback H⊗_B B_Y.

The following localized compactness observation is essential. If θ_{ξ,ζ} is a module rank-one map, its pullback is T_ξ T_ζ*, where T_ξ:b↦ξ⊗b is initially an adjointable creation map from B_Y. For g∈C_c(Y), T_ξ g is rectangular compact: its squared norm coefficient is |g|² h*<ξ,ξ>∈B_Y. Approximate identities of B_Y therefore approximate T_ξ g by the compact creation maps b↦(ξ⊗g e_n)b. Explicitly the error norm squared is bounded by ||(1−e_n)|g|²h*<ξ,ξ>(1−e_n)||→0. A central split of g into two square-root factors (first for nonnegative g) shows that the g-localized pullback of θ_{ξ,ζ} is compact. Finite sums and norm limits give every old compact map; real/imaginary parts and C0(Y) approximation give every base localization. This is why nonproper pullback preserves representable cycles even though it does not preserve global compactness without localization.

Source actions extend from the dense balanced algebra to its complete section algebra, using the faithful fibre norm. A new source coefficient on a compact Y support is approximated by finite sums of g times a pulled old coefficient. Choose u∈C_c(X) equal to one on h(supp g). The old localized defects tested by that u are compact. The observation above makes their pullbacks compact after g. All commutator, square and adjoint conditions therefore survive on the whole base-changed module. An adjointable operator pulls back as F⊗1 and has the same bound. This defines the geometric-field pullback without assuming h proper.

For the principal module the whole tensor map sends ξ⊗a to h*ξ·a. Its inner products are identical counting sums and convolution evaluated at h(y), so it is isometric in C0(Y,A) norm. Compact pullback chart supports admit finite separated-function approximations: cut off a compact neighbourhood of their image in X, cover by the relative anchor charts, and use a finite partition in Y. Functions on Y and pullbacks of local arrow-chart functions are dense on each compact product chart. The common Schur bound proves module-norm density; completion is onto. Finite Clifford modules and both Morita evaluations pull back literally. The raw Bott multipliers and both inverse homotopies also pull back literally on the base-changed algebras, with compact support estimates on the image of each compact Y set.

For the products in(392), product operators pull back by the same criterion, without an unavailable ordinary KK homomorphism. On a compact parameter support the pulled creation errors are compact by the rank-one observation and its rectangular version. Finite balanced creation sections are dense, treating all errors. Here is the required positivity check for arbitrary new source coefficients, including their cross terms. Denote the old even self-adjoint anticommutator by T. For a new coefficient a supported in a compact subset K⊂Y, choose u∈C_c(X), 0≤u≤1, equal to one on h(K). The old source is the nondegenerate finite Clifford bundle, so φ(u1_Cl) is precisely the right central multiplier u. The old criterion says uTu≥0 modulo K(H). Functional calculus in the Calkin algebra gives uTu=Q+J with Q≥0 adjointable and J compact: take Q=(uTu)_+ and J=−(uTu)_−. After pullback, a(h*T)a* equals a(h*Q)a* plus a(h*J)a*, since h*u=1 on its support. The first term is positive. Choose g∈C_c(Y) equal to one on K; the second is compact by the proved g-localized compact pullback. General C0 source coefficients are norm limits of compactly supported ones. This verifies the full criterion, rather than just its individual separated summands. The same argument applies to the first product, whose finite Clifford source is also essential. Products therefore have the actual pulled operators on the associating tensor-module unitary. The(392) module followed by the constant external η is the corresponding construction for fh, including the same right A representation. Product uniqueness gives

\[ h^*\chi_f(\eta)=\chi_{fh}(\eta) \tag{394} \]

with the full pulled Clifford twist. The average(393) pulls back by its finite intrinsic formula. For proper h the total-bundle map is proper as well, so this also recovers the actual C0 homomorphism comparison(146). Compact bases give the earlier compact smooth result. Properness has not been silently added to naturality in the geometric-field model.

Changing cocycle representatives uses the principal-space unitary from their actual equivalence arrows. Its products compose exactly on cores, and therefore on the completion. Its normal derivative transports the full Clifford twist. Start with the transported metric, then use the positive metric interpolation. For a continuous homotopy of actual cocycles on X×I, C2–C4 apply once to that whole base. Endpoint restrictions are onto: a compact endpoint core section extends in its relative product chart using a parameter cutoff, and finite chart sums are dense. This is the same complete module proof as6.0n, with a continuous parameter and vertical-smooth variables. The product theorem on the interval algebra then gives one homotopy of χ, rather than separately chosen endpoint operators.

For fixed germ data, normalized tube germs have a concrete contraction. In one reference tube, write another as a fibre-preserving germ h:E→E with h(x,0)=0 and D_vh(x,0)=1. Put

\[ h_s(x,v)=s^{-1}h(x,sv)\quad(s>0),\qquad h_0(x,v)=v. \tag{395} \]

The identity h_s(x,v)=∫_0^1 D_vh(x,tsv)v dt proves continuous extension at s=0, with all vertical derivatives. The derivatives at zero remain one, uniformly on any compact parameter set. The parameter inverse argument of C2 gives a common sufficiently small disk on that set; noncompact base patches use a positive continuous variable radius. Thus(395) is a contraction in normalized fibrewise smooth germs, fixed on the identity germ.

It also supplies finite relative extensions, with face data kept exactly as germs. Suppose compatible normalized germs are given on the boundary of a simplex. Use a collar of that boundary and extend by its collar retraction; keep those germs constant on the outer collar. On the inner collar apply(395) from that boundary value to the identity, using a scalar parameter equal to one near the outer collar and zero at its inner edge. Fill the remaining simplex by the identity. The integral formula and the uniform inverse radius make the extension continuous and fibre smooth. Metric boundary data extend in the same collar and interpolate through the convex cone of positive metrics to a fixed metric. Radii may always be shrunk by another positive minorant, because they specify representatives of the same germs. Refinements and representative comparisons have a common locally finite smaller germ neighbourhood by C2. Equivalence-arrow maps compose there exactly, so they add no associator defect.

Over that whole X×Δ^n, C3 and the product theorem give one module and one product operator. Restrictions to faces use the onto core restriction map and the naturality of the product class. The geometric tube and metric choices can therefore be filled in every finite dimension; their choices of representative germs have no finite-dimensional obstruction. These finite germ fillings compare entire family classes. The global construction in Q and D uses one separable base and one product module. Thus it does not require an infinite family of separately chosen Fredholm operators on simplicial faces.
