Q1. Open Euclidean sets have countable CW models with whole inverses

Let O⊂R^q be open. Cover it by the countably many open rational rectangular boxes whose closures are compact and lie in O. All nonempty finite intersections are convex boxes. Denote the cover by U_i and its abstract nerve by N. It has countably many simplices. Choose a locally finite partition ρ_i with closed support inside U_i. A countable locally finite precompact shrinking of the cover gives this partition; merging functions assigned to the same U_i retains local finiteness and closed subordination, as in A2. Put

\[ \Phi:O\to|N|,\qquad x\mapsto(\rho_i(x))_i. \tag{420} \]

Near a point only finitely many supports occur, and their common positive membership makes every used simplex a nerve simplex. Thus this is a whole continuous map in the weak CW topology.

For every nonempty nerve face S choose p_S∈∩_(i∈S)U_i. On a barycentric flag S_0⊊⋯⊊S_k define Ψ by the affine combination of p_(S_j) with that flag's weights. All these points lie in the convex intersection for S_0. The formula agrees on flag faces and defines a whole map Ψ:|N|→O. Here barycentric subdivision has its literal piecewise affine homeomorphism to |N|: it is a finite homeomorphism on each closed simplex, with compatible faces, and both global topologies are the weak simplex topologies.

The straight segment from x to ΨΦ(x) stays in O. Indeed, in the flag piece containing Φ(x), both x and all p_(S_j) belong to the intersection for S_0. The affine formula agrees on flag boundaries, giving the whole homotopy ΨΦ≃1_O.

For the other homotopy use the closed-star carrier of S_0 in N. It consists of faces T with T∪S_0 a nerve face. It contracts to any chosen vertex of S_0 by adjoining that vertex and linearly moving weight to it. Both the original flag simplex and ΦΨ of it lie in that carrier: Ψ lies in all U_i for i∈S_0, and its positive partition labels therefore form a face with S_0. On removing the first flag face the new carrier is the star of S_1, contained in the star of S_0; other faces keep the same carrier. Induct over the flag cells to extend the homotopy already given on their boundaries, fixed at its two ends. The boundary sphere map into the contractible carrier fills by its displayed cone contraction. This supplies the homotopy on each cell times I. The CW weak topology, and its product with I, prove continuity of the entire homotopy ΦΨ≃1_(|N|). Thus O has the countable CW model |N| with both whole inverse homotopies. The case q=0 is the one-point or empty complex and obeys the same statement.

Q2. The cellular-approximation input is proved here

We need to attach the CW models from Q1 along arbitrary transferred maps. The following supplies the needed cellular replacement. Any map of CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map, relative to a subcomplex on which it is already cellular.

First consider a map of a compact finite polyhedron of dimension n into R^m, m>n. On an open subset where it is allowed to change, it can be approximated within any given positive continuous error by a locally piecewise affine map missing a prescribed point. The error can tend to zero at the relative closed set, whose original map already misses the point. Here is the construction. An open subset of a finite polyhedron has a locally finite triangulation with simplices small enough for the prescribed error and the local oscillation of the map. To construct one, exhaust that subset by finite unions of small closed subdivided simplices with interiors covering it and closures inside it, subdivide successive collars further, and take their compatible subdivisions. Compact subsets meet only finitely many collars. Additional subdivisions on each collar give any specified mesh bound. This works separately on the finitely many original polyhedron faces, with their boundary subdivisions retained.

Choose each vertex image sufficiently near its original value. Avoid the finitely many affine dependence conditions that would put the prescribed point into the affine span of an incident simplex. Local finiteness makes the number of those incident simplices finite. Equivalently, choose successively outside their proper affine exceptional sets; for the last vertex of every simplex, the span of its earlier vertices and the prescribed point has dimension at most n<m. The resulting affine maps miss the point on every simplex, and their oscillation/error bound gives the stipulated approximation. Set the map equal to its original value on the relative closed set. The error tending to zero there proves continuity of the joined map and of the straight approximation homotopy. This construction also works inside an open ball: bound the error by half the distance of the old value to the ball boundary, as well as by the desired bound.

Now let b:D^n→Y be a map into a CW complex with boundary in Y^n. Its compact image meets finitely many cells by B4's finite cell argument; include their finite closures. Start with the highest dimensional cells of this finite subcomplex. If m>n, use the preceding approximation in the open m-cell, on its preimage, leaving the map outside that cell fixed. The error tends to zero at its preimage boundary, so the modification and its homotopy are continuous and fix ∂D^n. In its characteristic-ball coordinates choose the error also smaller than the distance to the sphere. The modified map misses the cell centre. Retract the punctured closed characteristic ball radially to its boundary, with the homotopy fixed on that sphere. Since the domain image is compact and avoids the centre, this induces a continuous homotopy of b through the finite CW quotient. It removes that open cell from the image. Remove all cells in decreasing dimension until the image lies in Y^n. There are finitely many of them. The boundary stays fixed throughout.

Induct on the cells of the source CW complex. In dimension n, the already constructed boundary homotopy is appended as a collar to the old characteristic disk map. Apply the just-proved relative disk step to its endpoint. The cell-cylinder retraction of R4 extends the homotopy while preserving the previously assigned boundary. On a designated relative subcomplex use the constant homotopy. The weak CW topology and its product with the interval make the resulting map and homotopy continuous on the whole complex. Its n-skeleton is now mapped into Y^n for every n. This proves the asserted cellular approximation, including the countable infinite complexes used next.

Q3. Fat cell assemblies of countable CW-type pieces

Suppose a one-fold or two-fold semisimplicial space has T1 levels, each a countable disjoint union of spaces with countable CW models and whole inverse homotopies. Its fat realization has a countable CW replacement with a specified weak equivalence. The two-fold case suffices here and includes the one-fold case.

The simultaneous quotient has pieces Z_(m,n)×Δ^m×Δ^n and only their face identifications in the two directions. Both iterated fat realizations are homeomorphic to it. A quotient remains quotient after product with either finite simplex, so the two orders of the quotients impose exactly this same final topology. Filter by total degree m+n. At degree N attach the countable disjoint union of Z_(m,n)×(Δ^m×Δ^n), m+n=N, along its boundary. The rectangle is a closed N-ball with its boundary an (N−1)-sphere. It has a literal collar (or a piecewise affine one after a finite triangulation), so R1's ordinary-attachment/double-cylinder comparison applies.

Inductively let e_(N−1):K_(N−1)→T_(N−1) be a homotopy equivalence from a countable CW model of that finite filtration. Replace the new Z pieces by their countable CW models L_N, and replace the old target by K_(N−1). Transfer the attaching map L_N×∂D^N→T_(N−1) through a chosen whole inverse of e_(N−1). Make that transferred map cellular using Q2. Attach L_N×D^N to K_(N−1) along it; call the result K_N. Products with the finite sphere/disk have the product CW structure. Each new open cell has dimension dim(cell of L_N)+N and its boundary lands in the appropriate lower skeleton because the attaching map is cellular. Closure finiteness follows because each such compact cell boundary meets finitely many old CW cells, and each product cell has finitely many product faces. Thus K_N is a countable CW complex containing K_(N−1) as a subcomplex.

There is an actual comparison e_N:K_N→T_N extending e_(N−1) literally. On a collar of the new disk boundary first follow the cellular-approximation homotopy, then the inverse comparison homotopy e_(N−1)e_(N−1)^−1≃1. The inner disk is mapped by the new piece comparison. The collar ends agree with both its attaching boundary and that inner disk. At degree0 just use the given model map for the disjoint degree0 pieces.

This comparison is a homotopy equivalence at each finite degree. The disk-collar comparison turns both attachments into double mapping cylinders. On the three span objects the chosen model maps are whole homotopy equivalences; the attaching squares commute by the collar's displayed homotopy. The homotopy-track proof of R1 applies also to this homotopy-commuting square: map the first part of the cylinder along its prescribed boundary track and the remainder along the actual cylinder. The inverse uses the inverse object maps and reversed tracks. In either composite adjacent reversed tracks contract by shortening the out-and-back intervals, and the remaining object inverse homotopies give the identity cylinder map. All formulas keep the old object map fixed at the cylinder end. This proves the finite-stage claim and the literal extension property of e_N; no level model maps compatible with all face maps were assumed.

Put K=∪_N K_N with its CW topology. The compatible maps e_N give a whole continuous e:K→T, since every CW cell occurs at a finite stage. It is a weak equivalence. A compact subset of K meets finitely many cells by B4, hence lies in some K_N. A compact subset of T has bounded minimal total degree: if not, select points of strictly increasing minimal total degrees. In each fixed (m,n) piece, the inverse image of a selected point is a finite union of closed sets, specified by its zero weights and the T1 point inverse images under the finitely many face maps. Only finitely many selected points can occur in that piece. The inverse image of any subset of the selected points is therefore closed in every piece. The weak quotient makes the selected set and all its subsets closed, producing an infinite closed discrete subspace of a compact space, a contradiction.

The finite filtration stages have their actual subspace topology. At each attachment the closed disk boundary is embedded and has a collar, so an open set of the old stage extends to an open set of the new stage by its open collar and the attaching map. Extending such opens inductively proves the same statement for a fixed stage in the weak infinite quotient. Thus a map whose image lies in a stage really factors continuously through that stage. Spheres, disks and homotopy cylinders on both sides can now be tested at finite stages. Their comparisons e_N are homotopy equivalences, proving that e induces the component bijection and all homotopy-group isomorphisms. This argument asserts a weak equivalence, and does not require coherent inverse homotopies on the non-CW infinite target.

Q4. A countable chart resolution for the actual étale nerve

For the smooth étale groupoid H of B1, N_n(H) is a second-countable locally Euclidean T1 space, possibly non-Hausdorff. Locally specify each arrow of a chain by a bisection and its source by a sufficiently small coordinate disk. This gives a chart parametrized by that source disk. Shrink it so every iterated face map is injective on the chart: the retained initial source is obtained by the appropriate initial composite of the finitely many bisection embeddings. There are only finitely many such composites. Every resulting face image is then a Hausdorff open chart in the lower nerve level. A countable bisection basis supplies countably many such chain charts covering every degree. Close their families under all face images. Countably many degrees and finite face operations still give countable families.

Let V_n be these actual open chart subsets, indexing equal subsets only once. A face carries V∈V_n to its literal image d_iV∈V_(n−1). The face equations hold also for these labels because images of composed maps are images under the composite. Let C_n be the open-cover groupoid of V_n on N_n(H), as in W4, and set

\[ Z_(m,n)=N_m(C_n) =\coprod_{(V_0,\ldots,V_m)}V_0\cap\cdots\cap V_m. \tag{421} \]

The cover faces delete labels; the H faces take their images and the actual nerve point. They commute literally, making Z a bisemisimplicial space. Repeated labels remain allowed. Each intersection is an open subset of the Hausdorff coordinate chart V_0, hence an open Euclidean set in that chart. Q1 gives each intersection a countable CW model with whole inverse homotopies. There are countably many label strings in every degree, so the same is true of the disjoint union Z_(m,n). These levels are T1.

W4 gives a weak augmentation ||N(C_n)||→N_n(H) for every n. Its domain is T1: the inverse of a point in each finite nerve piece is the finite closed face description used in Q3. These augmentations commute with all H faces, since every face keeps the underlying point's actual image. Apply W3 in the other direction. With the iterated/simultaneous quotient identification of Q3 it proves

\[ T=\|\!\|Z\|\!\|\longrightarrow B_f H \quad\hbox{is a weak equivalence}. \tag{422} \]

Q3's construction supplies a countable CW weak replacement e:K→T. Its composite k:K→B_f H is therefore a specific weak equivalence. This comparison is made using the actual nerve points and actual H faces. A contractible fibre, a stalkwise category argument or a thin-nerve degeneracy theorem was not substituted for the levelwise weak comparisons.

Q5. The universal actual cocycle on a locally compact replacement

Take a finite-subcomplex exhaustion of the countable K, including each cell's finite closure at a finite stage. Its telescope X is locally compact, Hausdorff and second countable, with the proper height and full homotopy equivalence p:X→K proved in B4. The B4 proof uses only countability and the CW structure, so it applies to this verified K. Define the whole map

\[ F_X=d k p:X\longrightarrow B_M H. \tag{423} \]

Pull back U1's actual cocycle, U2's explicit numerable partition and U3's full normal bundle. Call them f_X and E_X=F_X*E_M. They are genuine continuous data on this entire eligible X. In particular, E_X retains all normal transport, orientation and spin-c obstruction; its metric can be pulled back from U3. The resulting C_X Clifford algebra is separable, so (389)–(394) apply to one module over the whole base, rather than a sequence of independently chosen compact restrictions.

The map v F_X is homotopic to k p by the entire homotopy(415). Both are weak equivalences. By V6 their composite into B_f G is a specific weak equivalence as well. Thus X with f_X is a locally compact classifying CW replacement of the full holonomy groupoid, with its specified normal cocycle. This is the model used for the geometric twisted cohomology below. The maps retain the full X; no compact-stage inverse limit enters its definition.

Q6. Whole model independence, including prescribed comparison tracks

Suppose X and X' are two locally compact CW replacements made by this construction, with their specified weak maps F,F' to B_M H. W1 applied to F', on the entire CW complex X, gives h:X→X' and a whole homotopy F' h≃F. Applying W1 to F gives a map in the other direction. More precisely h is itself a weak equivalence by the homotopy and the two weak maps into B_M H; B4's full CW proof makes h a whole homotopy equivalence. Pull the U1 cocycle back along the displayed whole homotopy to X×I. It is a concordance between h*f_(X') and f_X, with the literal normal pullbacks at both ends.

The comparison is unique up to a whole homotopy carrying the prescribed map-to-B_M track. If h_0,h_1 have tracks from F'h_i to F, concatenate their tracks to give b:X×I→B_M H with endpoints F'h_0,F'h_1. W1 for the CW pair (X×I,X×{0,1}), with F' as its weak map, lifts b relative to those endpoints, giving a whole homotopy h_0≃h_1. The lift's comparison homotopy keeps both endpoint maps fixed. This is the full relative assertion of W1; it is not just agreement on each finite subcomplex of X. Composition of such comparisons has the same property, so their class maps are canonically compatible once the specified maps-to-B_M are retained.

Part D turns this complete cocycle/model comparison into the full twisted field-group comparison.

D1. Whole bundle transport along a compact parameter interval

Let E be a metrized rank-q real bundle over X×I, for eligible X. There is a continuous family of orthogonal isomorphisms E_(x,0)→E_(x,t), equal to the identity at t=0. We prove this on the entire noncompact X, rather than choosing unrelated compact transports.

A countable locally finite closed-subordinate partition for orthonormal bundle charts gives an isometric embedding into the trivial real ℓ² bundle: send a vector to its chart coordinates multiplied by the square roots of those partition functions. The squared norm is the original squared norm by their sum-one identity. Locally only finitely many terms occur. The range projection P(x,t) has rank q and is norm continuous; the same finite chart matrix calculation proves that continuity even when its nonzero coordinate list changes between neighbourhoods.

Extend P constantly at both interval ends. By compactness of I, continuity gives, near each x, a positive interval smoothing radius for which its oscillation is less than 1/8, uniformly in t. A locally finite shrinking and partition give a continuous positive minorant δ(x) for those allowed radii, using the minorant argument of C2. Convolve in t with a fixed smooth nonnegative compactly supported kernel of integral one and radius δ(x). The resulting self-adjoint Q(x,t) has ||Q−P||<1/8. It is continuous in x, continuously differentiable in t, and its derivative is locally bounded uniformly in t. Differentiation falls on the rescaled kernel, whose radius has a positive lower bound locally in x; there is no differentiation in x.

Its spectrum lies in the 1/8-neighbourhood of {0,1}. The spectral projection P~ for the interval near 1 is therefore continuously differentiable in t and continuous in x, by its resolvent contour formula. The distance to P is less than one, with an explicit bound. On range P~, Q has inverse norm at most 8/7, while ||(1−P)Q||<1/8; hence ||(1−P)P~||<1/7. On its complement apply the same argument to 1−Q and P, giving ||P(1−P~)||<1/7. The norm of the difference of orthogonal projections is the maximum of these two off-range norms, so ||P~−P||<1/7. Formula(424) consequently identifies their ranges and proves that P~ also has rank q. For two real orthogonal projections at distance less than one,

\[ U(A,B)=\bigl(AB+(1-A)(1-B)\bigr) \bigl(1-(A-B)^2\bigr)^{-1/2} \tag{424} \]

is an orthogonal operator taking range B to range A. Multiplication shows its first factor's square norm is 1−(A−B)^2; that positive operator commutes with both A and B. These identities prove the isometry and range assertions, while continuous functional calculus proves continuity. Thus U(P~,P) identifies the old and smoothed bundles continuously over the whole base.

Set A(x,t)=[∂_tP~,P~], a real skew-adjoint operator. Solve ∂_tV=A V with V(x,0)=1. Its Picard iterated integrals converge uniformly on I near each x, since A is locally uniformly bounded; the same estimates prove continuous dependence on x and t. Skew adjointness proves V*V=1, and solving the inverse equation proves onto-ness. Differentiating V*P~V gives zero: differentiating P~²=P~ makes ∂P~ off diagonal, and [P~,[∂P~,P~]]=−∂P~. Consequently V transports the smoothed initial range to the smoothed range at t. Combining with(424) at both ends gives the required whole orthogonal transport of E. All coefficients and operator norms above are real, so this construction does not choose a complex orientation or a spin-c lift.

Any two such transports starting at the identity differ by a continuous family of orthogonal automorphisms of E_0 starting at the identity. Their endpoint automorphisms are therefore homotopic through those automorphisms. The induced Clifford bundle isomorphisms have the same endpoint action on homotopy classes of cycles. The proof also works over X×J for every compact finite polyhedron J, with the transport interval retained as I. In particular it compares whole families of bundle paths.

D2. The full field group is homotopy invariant with its twist

For a metrized rank-q real bundle E over eligible X put

\[ \mathcal K^j(X;E) =KK_X^j\bigl(C_0(X,\operatorname{Cl}^{+}(E)^{op}),C_0(X)\bigr). \tag{425} \]

The opposite is the graded opposite, with the star and sign conventions of T2, hence its generators act as the negative right Clifford generators. By C4 this is exactly the group of whole Clifford–Fredholm fields: *-strong bounded operators, norm-continuous localized compact defects, and exact graded Clifford commutation. Both degrees use the ordered coefficient convention, retaining the positive right C1 in degree1. This statement includes every cycle and homotopy in the group, and not just the constructed χ.

Every continuous h:Y→X induces a pullback into K^j(Y;h*E) by C5's multiplier-valued balanced module tensor. It preserves localized compactness even for nonproper h. The associativity unitary on the balanced tensor modules gives (h k)*=k*h*; the creation-operator formulas identify the pulled fields and all their Clifford actions. It is additive and preserves degenerate cycles and whole homotopies, so is a group homomorphism.

For a constant bundle over X×I, its two endpoint maps agree on every class under the identification of the endpoints with E. A cycle over the whole interval is literally a KK_X homotopy with the right coefficient C0(X)⊗C(I). Restricting its left representation to the constant source gives that homotopy. Conversely its full interval source action is recovered from finite interval partitions, central right multipliers and compact base cutoffs as proved in C4. Thus its evaluations are the endpoint classes of the same homotopy, not independent fibre choices.

Moreover endpoint evaluation is an isomorphism with inverse constant pullback. One composite is literally the identity. For the other pull an arbitrary whole interval cycle back along r_s(x,t)=(x,(1−s)t), as a map from X×I×I to X×I. C5 applies to that whole eligible base. The source bundle is constant, so this is a genuine KK_(X×I) homotopy from the cycle to constant pullback of its zero evaluation. This proves the other composite is the identity on the full group. It does not assume a uniform operator norm homotopy of an arbitrary field; the whole-module topology is the one already proved in C4.

For a varying E on X×I use D1 to identify it with the pullback of E_0. The interval assertion just proved gives a group isomorphism between the endpoint twisted groups and equality of the transported endpoint classes of every whole cycle. Its choice is immaterial for this given bundle path: two D1 transports differ by the identity-started orthogonal family, and pulling a fixed cycle through its Clifford isomorphisms gives a whole homotopy of the corresponding endpoint actions. If the bundle paths are homotopic with fixed endpoint bundles, apply the construction on X×J×I. The endpoint transports form a continuous family in J. The two endpoint identifications are therefore the same on homotopy classes. This proves the relative parameter comparison needed for Q6's prescribed tracks.

It follows that a homotopy equivalence h with a specified normal-bundle comparison induces an isomorphism of(425). Apply the inverse map, retain the inverse homotopies and their pulled normal bundles, and use the preceding interval assertion to identify the two composites with the identity on the whole groups. No restriction of this proof to compact X is made.

D3. A precise full geometric cohomology convention on BG

Use the countable CW replacement of Q5 and its whole map F_X:X→B_M H. Its actual universal cocycle is f_X and its normal bundle is E_X. Define the full τ-twisted geometric cohomology by

\[ K^{j,\tau}(BG)=\mathcal K^j(X;E_X), \qquad j\in\mathbb Z/2. \tag{426} \]

Here BG means the full classifying homotopy type of the actual holonomy groupoid, with the universal derivative twist. V6 and Q5 supply its specific comparison to B_f G. This is a cocycle definition of cohomology: the fields, defects, equivalences and homotopies are those of C4, on one entire classifying CW model. The graded source in(425) specifies the rank and sign convention of τ explicitly; no orientation of τ is presumed. In a spin-c trivialization one can apply the full ordered Clifford/Morita evaluations of T2, but that is an additional reduction of these full groups, not part of their definition.

Q6 gives whole homotopy equivalences and actual normal concordances between any two such models. D2 gives the group isomorphisms and shows compatibility for their prescribed tracks, including their relative comparisons on X×I. Their compositions have the same property. Thus(426) is independent of the chosen countable chart resolution, Euclidean good covers, CW model, exhaustion, telescope, metric and specified replacement map, under those cocycle-compatible model comparisons. This includes all infinite classes on the whole X. It is not the group lim K^j(K_n;E_n), and no possible phantom or derived-limit information has been removed.

The statement concerns the classifying homotopy type on CW parameters, as represented by the verified CW replacement. It does not assert that arbitrary cohomology theories on an unreplaced non-CW topological quotient are weak-equivalence invariant. The cocycle, twist and full field convention in(426) are what specify the geometric group meant here.

D4. The single analytic-to-geometric class and its naturality

Keep A=C*r(G) for the original full holonomy groupoid. Apply (389)–(394) once to f_X on the whole X. This gives one countably generated module, its compact source action, both raw twisted Thom products and the single product

\[ \chi_X:KK^j(A,\mathbb C)\longrightarrow K^{j,\tau}(BG), \qquad \eta\longmapsto k_(f_X)\, \tau_(C_0(X))(\eta). \tag{427} \]

Additivity follows from the tensor module direct sums and the bilinearity of the proved product theorem0.6. Equivalent actual cocycles give the whole principal-space unitaries of C5. For a concordance on X×I, C2–C4 construct one whole product cycle; D2 identifies its two endpoints after their full normal transport. (394)'s finite tube/metric fillings prove choice independence in this whole construction. Thus χ_X is a group homomorphism, independent of its representative geometries.

For a model comparison h:X→X' with F'h≃F, C5 first gives h*χ_(X')(η)=χ_(h*f_(X'))(η). The actual cocycle concordance of Q6 and D2 then identify this class with χ_X(η). These are full-group identities. They prove that(427) gives a single χ with values in(426), independent of the model under its specified normal cocycle. In particular, it never replaces the analytical class by a Chern character, trace, numerical index or compact restrictions. Torsion classes enter the same product.

There is a useful universal test property. If an eligible locally compact CW base Y has an actual H-cocycle f, its whole Milnor map Φ_f exists by U4. W1 lifts Φ_f through the weak map F_X, producing a whole map a:Y→X and homotopy F_X a≃Φ_f. Pull back the actual U1 cocycle and its normal bundle along that homotopy. U4 identifies the other endpoint with f on its positive refinement. C5 and D2 therefore give

\[ a^*\chi(\eta)=\chi_f(\eta) \quad\text{in }\mathcal K^j(Y;f^*\tau), \tag{428} \]

with the normal comparison supplied by that whole homotopy. Different whole lifts with their specified comparison tracks are related by W1 on the relative CW pair Y×I, and D2 treats their bundle paths. Thus the test identity is independent of those lift choices. B1 translates it to actual G-cocycles using short plaque arrows, retaining the same algebra A in the analytic argument.

This construction avoids an infinite system of separately chosen Fredholm product operators on simplicial faces. It uses exactly one separable base algebra and one product module. All parameter naturality is obtained from this one entire product class.

G0. The two manifold cycles and their full analytic providers

Let M be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of dimension d, with a Riemannian metric. Put C=C(M), Q=C(M,Cl^+(TM)^op). Its real generators are negative: r(v)^*=-r(v), r(v)^2=-|v|². No orientation or spin-c structure on M is assumed. Disconnected components and dimension0 are treated by the same finite sum.

G1. The actual diagonal coevaluation cycle

Choose r>0 with the closed geodesic 2r disks inside the injective normal neighbourhood, uniformly on compact M. Put U={(x,y):x=exp_y(w), |w|<r}. Write

\[ q_r(v)=r v/\sqrt{1+|v|^2},\quad v=q_r^{-1}(w)=w/\sqrt{r^2-|w|^2}. \tag{429} \]

The coevaluation module is H_Θ=C0(U,pr_y*Cl^+(TM)^op), an ideal Hilbert C⊗Q module with its standard right inner product. The source ℂ is the scalar unital representation. Its odd operator is

\[ B_Θ(x,y)=i r_y(v_y(x))/\sqrt{1+|v_y(x)|^2}. \tag{430} \]

It is self-adjoint, of norm at most1, and its square defect is −1/(1+|v|²), a C0(U) section. The compact endomorphism algebra of this ideal module is the ideal itself, so the scalar-localized defect is compact. Source commutators vanish. Separability gives countable generation. This defines Θ∈KK(C_scalar,C⊗Q). It is the actual raw standard Clifford Bott cycle on the normal disk, using the *-isomorphism c^+(v)↦i r(v), followed by open extension. Tube compression and its two-sided inverse products are the full raw constructions6.0a–d, before orientation reduction. Different small radii and metrics give the same class by their normalized tube homotopies. The direction is from y to x in(430); this choice fixes the Gaussian sign in G4.

G2. The actual evaluation cycle

On H_D=L²(M,ΛT*M_C) use exterior-degree parity and the metric identification of tangent/cotangent. Write L_i=ε_i+ι_i, R_i=ε_i−ι_i. Q acts by R_i, and the extra C factor acts by pointwise multiplication at the same point. Define

\[ D=-i(d-d^*),\qquad F_D=D(1+D^2)^{-1/2}. \tag{431} \]

Here d is the exterior derivative; d* its actual metric adjoint. D is symmetric on smooth forms, with principal symbol L(ξ), and D²=d d*+d* d is the Hodge Laplacian. The complete-source energy argument, followed by elliptic regularity on the compact manifold, gives self-adjointness on its first-order Sobolev domain. The local compact-frequency estimate and a finite partition give compact resolvent. Smooth Q sections graded-commute with its principal symbol; their graded commutators with D are bounded zeroth-order operators. Formula(132), its convergent transform integral and density prove compact graded commutators with F_D. Its square defect is the compact resolvent−(1+D²)^−1. Thus

\[ \operatorname{ev}=[H_D,\rho,F_D] \in KK(Q\widehat\otimes C,\mathbb C). \tag{432} \]

These conventions are internally fixed, rather than inferred from a right-multiplication symbol in another convention. For comparison with the raw positive-left cycle D_raw=ΣR_i∂_i, the canonical even unitary on exterior degree k is (-i)^k. It takes L_i to −iR_i and R_i to−iL_i. Precompose the raw positive-left source by r_i↦i c_i^+. Its action becomes R_i and its Dirac becomes −iΣL_i∂_i, exactly(431)'s principal local form. This checks the graded opposite, its involution and the physical Fourier sign. It does not assert an unchecked identity with i r(ξ)ε from a different right-multiplication convention.

G3. The tube product lemma, with one complete operator family

We give the analytic deformation used in both triangles. After tensoring(430) with(432), the actual module is a field of L² sections on the geodesic r disks about its remaining base point. The first triangle has right coefficient C; the second has right coefficient Q. Smooth compact tube sections give the isometric dense tensor identification, with the old counting reduced to the ordinary pointwise C/Q fibre actions. In particular the tensor module is completed before this identification is used.

Use(429), the exact half-density Jacobian and metric parallel transport along the radial geodesics to identify these fields unitarily with L²(T_zM,ΛT_zM_C), with the appropriate right coefficient. Compact M and the closed 2r tube give uniform smooth coefficient bounds. The transformed Dirac principal matrix A_z(v) is invertible and has positive determinant, with A_z(0) a positive scalar matrix. Its polar orthogonal part is in SO(T_zM). Lift it along s↦O_z(sv), starting at1, to the even left Clifford Spin operators, as in the proved radial-lift construction7.23. This construction is orthogonally equivariant, hence global even when TM is nonorientable. Left even Spin operators commute with the negative right action R_i. They leave the source Q action and its full twist unchanged. Conjugation makes the principal matrix positive symmetric.

Multiply the transformed symmetric Dirac by the positive scalar ψ(v)=(1+|v|²)^−2, symmetrically on both sides. Its bounded phase has exactly the old Dirac principal phase on each compact tube chart: positive scalar multiplication does not change that phase. In coordinates the resulting symmetric operator is

\[ A_1=-\frac i2\sum_{ij}L_i (K_{ij}(v)\partial_j+\partial_j K_{ij}(v))+Z(v), \tag{433} \]

where K is positive symmetric, smooth and bounded with bounded first derivatives; Z is bounded odd self-adjoint. Indeed the inverse derivative of q_r grows at most C(1+|v|²)^(3/2), and its derivatives and half-density terms have at most that growth. The smooth exponential, transport and Spin coefficients are bounded on the closed 2r tube. The chosen ψ cancels that growth, including its derivative terms. K is uniformly positive on each bounded fibre ball. All assertions are uniform in the compact base charts and orthogonally equivariant.

Set K_s=(1−s)1+sK, Z_s=sZ and let A_s be(433) with these coefficients. In the first triangle set B(v)=−iR(v); in the second set B(v)=iΓ⊗r(v), where Γ is exterior parity and the last r is the target Q generator. Put T_s=A_s+B(v). These are symmetric odd complete operators on the single whole interval module. Their complete self-adjoint domains can be verified directly. On compact fibre sets ellipticity gives first-order local regularity. Cutoffs ρ_R have ||[T_s,ρ_R]||≤C/R, because the principal coefficients are bounded and the potential commutes with scalar cutoffs. For a deficiency solution T_s*u=±iu, the imaginary part tested against ρ_R²u gives ||ρ_Ru||²≤(C/R)||u||². Let R tend to infinity to obtain u=0 for both signs. This proves self-adjointness on the closure of the smooth compact core. For the whole module, the fibre resolvents are bounded by1 and strongly continuous, with their adjoints, on continuous compact-core inputs: approximate an input by a resolvent image at one parameter, use the common core and coefficient continuity there, then extend by the uniform resolvent bound. Local finite frames and a base partition give that assertion on the entire Hilbert bundle. Thus they define adjointable R_± on the whole parameter module. Their ranges are dense: the fibre ranges are dense, and finite base partitions patch their local norm approximations of a compact base section; base cutoffs treat every section. The two inverse identities, R_+*=R_− and their commutation hold as whole module identities, by the faithful fibre norms. The resolvent-domain argument of8.15a then proves regular self-adjointness, with R_+R_− the dense-range inverse of1+T_s². Fibre cutoffs and the local elliptic core give the same closed graph as the smooth compact core. This constructs the regular closure on the single whole parameter module.

The needed uniform compactness and continuity also follow from a concrete energy estimate. The anticommutator of A_s with B has bounded principal cross term and a zeroth term bounded by C(1+|v|). Therefore, as quadratic forms on the core,

\[ T_s^2\ge A_s^2+\tfrac12|v|^2-C'. \tag{434} \]

It bounds the v-tail of a resolvent vector uniformly. On a fixed fibre ball, local ellipticity of A_s bounds its first Sobolev norm uniformly in the compact parameters. The compact spatial/frequency estimate therefore gives finite-rank approximations uniformly after that ball cutoff. Tail first, then frequency, proves compact module resolvents. Core resolvent continuity and the uniform bound ||(T_s±i)^−1||≤1 give strong continuity; the uniform finite-rank approximations and their adjoints turn it into compact-operator norm continuity. Thus the bounded transforms of T_s are one KK homotopy, with compact defects on the entire interval module. No uniform positive lower bound for K at fibre infinity has been assumed; the confining estimate and local ellipticity are what prove compactness.

At s=1 this bounded transform is the actual product operator. For a homogeneous smooth compact tube creation section ξ, its Dirac leading phase agrees with the evaluation phase, with the factor(-1)^|ξ| in the connection error. The unbounded potential and Z are bounded on that compact section support and change only lower-order terms. Hence the two connection errors have order−1 locally. The complete compact-frequency proof6.1 makes them rectangular compact; finite parameter partitions give the module assertion, and norm density treats every ξ.

For the first-factor positivity let B_0=B/√(1+|v|²), precisely the tensor of(430). The derivative of this bounded potential is bounded, its leading part anticommutes with the Dirac part, and Z is bounded. Consequently

\[ \{T_1,B_0\}=2|v|^2/\sqrt{1+|v|^2}+J_0, \qquad ||J_0||\le C_0. \tag{435} \]

The graded integral identity(132) expresses the anticommutator with T_1(T_1²+q²)^−1 as q²R_q {T_1,B_0}R_q+T_1R_q {T_1,B_0}T_1R_q. Its negative part is bounded below by−C_0R_q. Each R_q is module compact and ∫_0^∞||R_q||dτ is finite, q²=1+τ². The identity here is a quadratic-form identity before its bounded extension, since the positive part of(435) grows like |v|. Estimate(434) makes that part bounded on the graph of T_1. The bounded smooth B_0 preserves that graph: T_1B_0=−B_0T_1+C on the core, with C={T_1,B_0} graph bounded. Thus the two-pole resolvent calculation proving(132) applies on the graph domain, and its sandwiched expressions extend boundedly by the same energy estimate. This justifies its use without claiming that C itself is globally bounded. Integrating finite intervals, then taking the strict transform limit, shows positivity modulo module compacts: the negative compact majorants converge in norm and their tails tend to zero. This argument does not require norm convergence of the separate positive unbounded-potential integrals. It proves the full bounded product positivity criterion. Both conditions are now checked on the actual completed product module.

After deforming to s=0, contract the source point along exp_z(t q_r(v)), from its old tube point to z, and transport its full Clifford source along that same radial path. Smooth source sections have uniformly bounded derivatives and bounded commutators with the flat T_0; density gives the entire source algebra. The transported Q action is the negative right action R at z, since the left Spin gauge was even and commuted with it. The exact radial source homotopy is norm continuous on each smooth source section, uniformly on the closed tube. Compact resolvents make every resulting localized defect compact. This is a whole KK homotopy to the constant source at z, not an independently chosen homotopy at each base point.

G4. The function-algebra triangle is exactly its even Gaussian line

In (Θ⊗1_C)(1_C⊗ev) the remaining target base is x and the integration point is y. Reversing the radial geodesic gives PT_(y→x)log_y(x)=−log_x(y), and(429) is odd and preserves the radial norm. Thus its flat operator has the exact sign

\[ T_C=-i\sum_i(L_i\partial_i+R_i v_i),\qquad T_C^2=-\Delta+|v|^2+\sum_i(2N_i-1). \tag{436} \]

Here N_i=ε_iι_i is the occupancy projection. The one-dimensional oscillator spectrum follows by factoring ∂+v and its adjoint; its vacuum is exp(−v²/2), its raising operators generate all Hermite functions, and their density is the complete oscillator argument already supplied in6.0c. Hence the unique ground space of(436) is the normalized Gaussian times the exterior vacuum1, in even degree. All other eigenvalues are at least2. Both the Gaussian and its vacuum are orthogonally invariant, so that kernel line is globally the trivial even C module. After G3's source contraction the source f acts by f(x) on it.

On the complement replace the bounded transform by sign(T_C) along the straight functional-calculus homotopy, retaining zero on the kernel. The gap makes this bounded continuous. Its square defects remain compact, and its source commutators are zero after the source contraction. At the end the complement is a degenerate cycle; the remaining kernel is (C,identity,0). Therefore the first triangle is exactly

\[ (\Theta\widehat\otimes1_C) (1_C\widehat\otimes\operatorname{ev})=1_C. \tag{437} \]

The tensor positions in(437) put Θ's function factor first, its Q factor second, and the old C source last. There is no odd permutation hidden in this typed expression.

G5. The Clifford-algebra triangle is its entire regular module

In (1_Q⊗Θ)(ev⊗1_Q) the remaining target base is y and the integration point is x. The normal vector points from y to x, so the target potential has the opposite sign to G4's reversed radial vector. The target odd operator includes the graded tensor sign exactly once:

\[ T_Q=-i\sum_i L_i\partial_i+i\Gamma\otimes r(v),\qquad T_Q^2=-\Delta+|v|^2+\sum_i S_i, \quad S_i=L_i\Gamma\otimes r_i. \tag{438} \]

Each S_i is a self-adjoint involution. They commute: both its exterior factors and its two negative r factors anticommute for distinct indices. Their joint−1 eigenspace is a free rank-one right Q module. Its explicit even unit vector is

\[ \Omega=2^{-d/2}\sum_{I\subset\{1,\ldots,d\}} (-1)^{|I|(|I|+1)/2}e_I\otimes r_I. \tag{439} \]

In fact Ω=2^(d/2)∏_i(1−S_i)/2 applied to the exterior vacuum⊗1. Expanding the commuting product gives(439): moving the intervening Γ's past the successive L's contributes (-1)^(k(k−1)/2), and its k minus signs contribute(-1)^k. Its inner product is 2^−d sum_I r_I* r_I=1. The equations S_iΩ=−Ω follow from the product. Conversely those equations determine every exterior coefficient from its vacuum coefficient, so Ω Q is their entire joint−1 eigenspace. There is no other ground block, in any dimension.

Most importantly, direct insertion/removal of i in the ordered words gives

\[ (R_i\otimes1)\Omega=\Omega r_i. \tag{440} \]

The negative square r_i²=−1 supplies the removal sign, and the exponent in(439) supplies precisely the creation sign. Thus this is the identity left Q representation on the kernel, not merely a rank-one module with an unspecified Clifford action. The formula is globally orthogonally equivariant: the joint projector, vacuum and Clifford products transform together. No frame, orientation or spin-c line was selected to glue it.

Multiplying Ω by the normalized Gaussian gives the exact entire kernel of(438); all other energies are at least2. It is a free even right Q module with the identity source action by(440), after G3's whole source contraction. Replace the bounded transform by its sign on the complement just as in G4. Its exact graded source commutation makes that complement degenerate. Consequently

\[ (1_Q\widehat\otimes\Theta) (\operatorname{ev}\widehat\otimes1_Q)=1_Q. \tag{441} \]

The target r in(438) is represented by Γ⊗r, while the source r acts by R⊗1. Keeping those two distinct actions is essential for(440). Both triangles are even KK equalities before any parity reduction. Tensoring a positive right C1 in its prescribed final position retains that order and gives the same two products in odd degree. Any later spin-c reduction uses the complete even Morita evaluations, so no determinant-line replacement or scalar trace can alter these proved identities. In dimension0 the sums and potential vanish, Ω=1, and both triangles are the pointwise identities on the finite component set.

H1. The entire orientation cap, with its necessary reflection

Let M be compact smooth without boundary, C=C(M), W=TM, E=f*τ, d=rank W, q=rank E, m=d+q. Write A_L=C(M,Cl⁺(W⊕E)) and P_L=C(M,Cl⁺(W⊕E)ᵒᵖ)=P_W ⊗_C P_E. This is the graded opposite with negative real generators and its actual involution T2. The ordered real list is W first, E second. Let S:A_L ↝ C⊗C_m be the prescribed entire even imprimitivity module. Its scalar transition line is part of S. At rank zero retain the full graded line, including an odd line if specified.

Let γ_L be the grading automorphism of A_L: it sends every real positive generator to its negative. Set S^γ equal to S with left action precomposed by γ_L. This retains its underlying right module, Hermitian metric, scalar transitions and grading. It is an actual module, not a determinant-line replacement.

Put Z=Λ(W⊕E)_C. Its actions L_i=ε_i+ι_i and R_i=ε_i−ι_i give A_L ⊗_C P_L = End_C(Z), with both full Morita evaluations as in T2–T3. Let z=[Z]:A_L⊗_C P_L→C. Define

\[ t_S=z^{-1}(S^\gamma\widehat\otimes_C1_{P_L})\,\beta \in RKK_M(C,P_W\widehat\otimes_C P_E\widehat\otimes C_m). \tag{442} \]

Here β is the actual graded right coefficient transport from C_m,P_L to P_L,C_m. Each interchange of homogeneous vectors has its Koszul sign. The last positive C_m is retained in its specified order. Every factor is an even full imprimitivity module, so H1 has both inverse Morita products. Its concrete zero-operator module is the conjugate Z* balanced with S^γ⊗P_L, then transported by β. Local finite frames and partitions prove compact left C action and right fullness. The construction uses the entire given module; a line H tensored with S passes through as the same H, not H*.

The reflection γ_L is essential. An unreflected dual cap transposes a positive generator to its negative in this graded opposite convention. H2 verifies the actual sign on the whole finite module before any degree reduction.

H2. Full finite evaluation and its physical generators

To check H1, choose an ordered real orthonormal frame and a principal frame of S, so its right module is C_m. Write e_I for the exterior monomial and c_I for the increasing positive Clifford word. First balance H1 with the forms Z carrying the negative left P_L action R. The external positive C_m action on this second factor is Γ_Z⊗c; its position is last. On the resulting right C_m module define

\[ U(\overline {e_I}\otimes e_J) =2^{-m/2}(-1)^{|I|(|J|+1)+|I|(|I|-1)/2}c_Jc_I. \tag{443} \]

The suppressed S frame is its regular unit. All homogeneous right coefficients are placed in their stated final position. This formula is checked against both balances, rather than assuming that a same-rank module has the desired action.

On Z*, right a_i is the adjoint-dual of L_i and right r_i is the adjoint-dual of R_i, hence −R_i. The reflection in S^γ gives the first relation below; the second is the negative-source balance:

\[ \begin{split} U(\overline {L_i w}\otimes v) &=-(-1)^{|v|}U(\bar w\otimes v)c_i,\\ U(-\overline {R_i w}\otimes v) &=U(\bar w\otimes R_i v). \end{split}\tag{444} \]

Inserting or removing i in increasing words proves both equations: the removal sign of R differs from that of L, and c_i²=1. Starting at I=empty, the second equation and then the first give U(bar1⊗e_J)=2^−m/2 c_J and exactly H2 for every I. Thus H2 is defined on the entire balanced tensor, not only a corner.

Its inner product can be checked directly. The right inner product on Z* is θ_(w,w'), represented by the faithful full matrix algebra L(A_L)R(P_L). Its vacuum projection is ∏_i(1+L_iR_i)/2. After the reflection and β, its action on Z⊗C_m has vacuum coefficient 2^−m; all nonempty words send the exterior vacuum to an orthogonal word. Consequently ζ=2^(m/2)(bar1⊗1) has <ζ,ζ>=1. Relations H3 reduce every tensor to ζc. They therefore show that the entire inner product is c*c' and that U is an onto right-linear even unitary. Equivalently, expanding each θ_(e_I,e_I') in the complete L_AR_B matrix basis gives <U_(I,J),U_(I',J')> term by term; there is no discarded compact-algebra corner.

The physical positive operator on the forms factor has the tensor grading once: bar e_I⊗v maps to (-1)^|I| bar e_I⊗L_i v. H2 now gives

\[ U\bigl((-1)^{|I|}\bar e_I\otimes L_i e_J\bigr) =c_i U(\bar e_I\otimes e_J). \tag{445} \]

It suffices also to check this on ζ: r_i sends the first vacuum to −bar e_i, while reflected a_i moves that bar e_i to minus the final c_i. The two minus signs cancel. Thus the induced physical generator is precisely c_i, not −c_i. Both W and E blocks keep their original order in H4.

These maps glue. Exterior transitions act on Z and Z* by the actual dual orthogonal maps and fix their vacua. The reflection commutes with every even principal spin-c transition. The resulting coefficient map has exactly S's real Clifford transition and its scalar phase z; the whole unitary is built from those finite evaluations. It therefore retains an arbitrary line twist and a two-torsion line. For m=0 the contraction is the scalar evaluation tensored with the entire graded S line. Smooth compact parameter families use these same maps on their bundle over M×J. H2–H4 and both full Morita evaluations hold on that entire parameter bundle.

H3. The full test class and exact KK factorization

Let d_M∈KK(P_W,ℂ) be G2's evaluation restricted along a↦a⊗1 into P_W⊗C(M). It is the actual negative-source de Rham cycle, not a separately chosen spin-c Dirac class. For any a∈RKK_M^j(P_E,C), compose t_S with 1_(P_W)⊗_C a, keep the final positive C_m, forget base linearity, and compose with d_M externally over the retained coefficients. The domain after forgetting is C(M). This defines a full class

\[ \mathsf{cap}_S(a)\in KK(C(M),C_j\widehat\otimes C_m), \qquad C_0=\mathbb C, C_1=\operatorname{Cl}_1^+. \tag{446} \]

For j=0 the retained list is simply C_m. For j=1 it is C_1 from a, followed by C_m from the first cap. This is the native second-cycle-first list. Reducing m's even consecutive pairs and then the remaining ordered odd pair is exactly Section 0.13/7.20–7.21, not an ungraded permutation. The resulting scalar degree is j+m≡j+q−d mod2. Fullness, finite coefficients and the proved product theorem ensure existence over the actual whole M algebra in every case.

Apply the same construction to T5's k_f with coefficient A:

\[ y_f=\mathsf{cap}_S(k_f)\in KK(C(M),A\widehat\otimes C_m). \tag{447} \]

For η∈KK^j(A,ℂ), (388) and full external-coefficient associativity give

\[ \mathsf{cap}_S(\chi_f(\eta))=y_f\cdot\eta. \tag{448} \]

Here the product on the right includes the stated final C_j,C_m transport before parity reduction. To verify (448), retain the balanced chain t_S,(1_(P_W)⊗k_f),d_M,η. Move only the independent A-coefficient η past d_M by the graded external tensor interchange, then use the associating module unitaries of Section 0.9 and the two finite evaluations0.12. η acts on the A coefficient and d_M on P_W; the interchange has the degree-zero d_M and the actual displayed Clifford transport. The operator classes agree by the complete product uniqueness0.6. This proves equality of full KK classes before taking a scalar index.

For a Hermitian test bundle B over M, let [B]∈KK(C,C) be its complete finite zero-operator coefficient cycle. Multiplication by the unit u:ℂ→C(M) gives u[B]cap_S(χ_f(η))=u[B]y_f·η in scalar degree j+q−d. In even degree Section 0.14 takes its integral kernel-minus-cokernel index; in odd degree KK^1(ℂ,ℂ)=K_1(ℂ)=0. Neither the cap nor (448) quotients by torsion or passes to a character.

Metric, orientation-family and tube changes are whole families: T/C provide k_f over M×I, D1 transports its normal bundle, and H1's finite tensors and G's evaluation occur on the same coefficient interval. Their complete product homotopy gives the endpoint equality with the supplied full module paths. There is no claim of invariance after dropping that path.

H4. Two complete native calibrations

If M is a point, d_M=1 and H2–H4 identify (447) with the given spin-c reduced raw transverse Thom class followed by the actual étale correspondence L_f. Indeed the raw positive operator L_E(v) on forms is taken exactly to c_S(v) by H4; the compact creation connections and positivity 2B² of T4–T5 are preserved by the entire finite unitary. This is the native point-source wrong-way class of Section 6.0o, with all positive odd coefficient reductions in their given order. An even line H multiplies both by H; rank zero retains its entire graded line and its exact index sign.

If the target is the unit groupoid of a point, E=0 and L_f is the identity C(M) correspondence. H2–H4 take the evaluation's principal positive L_W symbol to c_S(ξ). Connections differentiated under this smooth finite bundle unitary add only zeroth-order terms. The complete compact manifold symbol quotient and negative-order estimate therefore identify (447) with the entire positive spin-c Dirac class a_p of Section 7.1, including its right C_d. The prescribed structure on W is exactly the one obtained from L=W by 7.18 with zero horizontal double. Section 7.22, whose full ordinary normal and native inverse calculation was supplied and read, gives y_f=p_!^geom. Thus (448) is the existing integral wrong-way pairing for this entire ordinary compact-manifold case, with all lines, finite bundles, rank-zero grading and both degrees.

Part I proves the general graph-normal class equality, beyond these two special calibrations.

E1. From every odd cycle to an honest compression extension

Let A be any separable complex C*-algebra, not necessarily unital or nuclear. Under the course's positive right C1 convention, an odd cycle is (H⊗C1,φ,F⊗ε), where H is separable, φ is an ordinary even representation, and F is self-adjoint. This follows by taking the even module summand; right multiplication by ε identifies the other summand with it. An odd right-linear operator then has exactly this form. Use the localized normalization from Section0 to take ||F||≤1. It satisfies [F,φ(a)] compact and (F²−1)φ(a) compact for every a. Neither defect is asserted globally compact when A has no identity.

Put s=(1−F²)^(1/2). Then sφ(a) and φ(a)s are compact. Indeed in the Calkin algebra q(F) commutes with qφ(A), and (1−q(F)²)qφ(a)=0. Continuous functional calculus in that commuting algebra gives q(s)qφ(a)=0; adjoints give the other side. This is a localized assertion and suffices. On H⊕H with representation π=diag(φ,0), define

\[ F_t=\begin{pmatrix}F&t s\\t s&-F\end{pmatrix}, \quad0\le t\le1,\qquad F_1^2=1. \tag{449} \]

Since F commutes with s, the square has diagonal F²+t²s². Its defects tested by π(a) are compact, and the off-diagonal commutators are ±t sφ(a), ±t φ(a)s. Thus E1 is a whole norm-continuous Kasparov homotopy. The second summand at t=0 has zero representation and is degenerate. Every odd class is therefore represented by an honest self-adjoint involution, without adding a global Fredholm assumption to a nonunital cycle.

Set P=(1+F_1)/2 and K=P(H⊕H). Compression gives a completely positive contraction σ(a)=Pπ(a)P|_K. Its multiplicative defect is

\[ \sigma(ab)-\sigma(a)\sigma(b) =P\pi(a)(1-P)\pi(b)P\in\mathcal K(K). \tag{450} \]

Here [P,π(a)] is compact, since it is half the original involution commutator. Consequently τ=q_Kσ is a *-homomorphism A→Q(K)=B(K)/K(K). The pullback algebra {(a,T):q_K(T)=τ(a)} gives an extension by K(K), and a↦(a,σ(a)) is its completely positive contractive section. Adding a zero Busby summand on ℓ² makes the ideal the standard infinite compact algebra if necessary. Degenerate or noninjective Busby maps are allowed; analytic K-homology does not require an essential extension.

E2. A complete dilation and the inverse cycle

Conversely, let τ:A→Q(H) admit a completely positive contractive lift σ:A→B(H). We construct its dilation here. On A⊙H use <a⊗ξ,b⊗η>=<ξ,σ(a*b)η>. Complete positivity gives positivity of every finite tensor sum. Quotient its null space and complete to K_0. Left multiplication defines π_0:A→B(K_0): the inequality ||b||²1−b*b≥0 in the unitization, inserted between each pair of tensor coefficients, proves ||π_0(b)||≤||b||. Adjoints are left multiplication by b*, so it is a *-representation. Its range is essential on K_0.

For a contractive approximate identity e_n, the vectors e_n⊗ξ have norm at most ||ξ||. On the dense tensor span their inner products converge to <a⊗η,V_0ξ>=<η,σ(a*)ξ>. This defines a bounded linear functional and hence a unique vector V_0ξ by the Hilbert space Riesz theorem. It gives a contraction V_0:H→K_0. The approximate-identity limits show V_0*π_0(a)V_0=σ(a). Indeed π_0(a)(e_n⊗ξ)=a e_n⊗ξ converges in norm to a⊗ξ, so π_0(a)V_0ξ=a⊗ξ. Pair this with V_0η by the defining Riesz formula to obtain the asserted compression identity. Separability of A and H makes K_0 separable.

On K=K_0⊕H take π=π_0⊕0 and the isometry Vξ=(V_0ξ,(1−V_0*V_0)^(1/2)ξ). Then V*π(a)V=σ(a) and V*V=1. Put P=VV* and F=2P−1. For C_a=(1−P)π(a)V, direct multiplication gives

\[ C_a^*C_a=\sigma(a^*a)-\sigma(a^*)\sigma(a) \in\mathcal K(H). \tag{451} \]

The quotient multiplicativity of τ gives the last inclusion. A bounded Hilbert space operator T with T*T compact is compact: cut its positive spectrum above a positive threshold to get finite-rank approximations and use the norm bound on the remaining spectrum. Therefore C_a is compact. The adjoint argument with a* gives both off-diagonal blocks of [P,π(a)] compact. F is an honest involution, so (K⊗C1,π,F⊗ε) is an odd Kasparov cycle. Its compression onto PK=VH gives exactly the original σ and τ, under V. No nuclearity or arbitrary extension-splitting theorem was used.

E3. Both constructions are inverse, including whole homotopies

To compare two isometric dilations of the same lift, adjoin the identity representation of A^+ to their representations. Let K_min be the closed span of π(A^+)VH. It reduces π, contains VH, and the projection P is zero on its complement. Its orthogonal complement therefore has F=−1 and is a degenerate cycle. On K_min the map

\[ \sum_i\pi(a_i)V\xi_i\longmapsto \sum_i\pi'(a_i)V'\xi_i \tag{452} \]

is an onto isometry, since its inner product is exactly Σ_(i,j)<ξ_i,σ^+(a_i*a_j)ξ_j>, where σ^+(a+λ1)=σ(a)+λ1. This unitization is completely positive by the actual isometric dilation just constructed: π^+(a+λ1)=π(a)+λ1 compresses to that formula. E4 intertwines π, V and P. Thus it gives an actual cycle unitary after removal of degenerate summands.

Starting from an involution Fredholm cycle, the original (π,inclusion of PH) is already an isometric dilation of its compression. E4 identifies the returned cycle with it, up to its degenerate complement. Starting from an extension, E2 returns precisely its original Busby map. These prove both inverse statements, not only surjectivity.

Two cpc lifts of the same τ differ by compact operators. Their convex path σ_t is cpc, and its multiplicative defects are norm-continuous compact functions of t. The same tensor construction over C(I), with inner products given by σ_t^+, gives one countably generated Hilbert C(I)-module, isometric V and projection P. Its off-diagonal construction uses A^+⊙C(I,H), π by left multiplication, and Vξ=1⊗ξ. Complete positivity is pointwise positivity of every continuous matrix σ_t^+; V*V=1 follows from σ_t^+(1)=1. Thus V is adjointable with V*(a⊗ξ)=σ_t^+(a)ξ, directly on the dense tensor core. No Hilbert-module Riesz representation theorem is assumed. The projection is VV*, and its off-diagonal operators C_a are rectangular module compact because C_a*C_a is compact in C(I,K). The module version of the preceding compactness argument uses the compact maps T(T*T)(T*T+δ)^−1. Functional calculus bounds their distance from T by sup_(λ≥0) √λ δ/(λ+δ)=√δ/2, tending to zero. Thus it is a whole Kasparov homotopy.

Conversely, do E1 and the projection compression on any odd KK homotopy module over C(I). Every defect lies in its entire module compact ideal. The projected module is complemented and countably generated. Add the standard C(I) module with zero Busby map and use the explicit stabilization unitary proved in Section 0.2. Its compact ideal becomes C(I,K); compression is a whole semisplit extension homotopy, not a separately selected extension at each t. The same procedure handles direct sums and ordinary unitary equivalence.

Adding a split extension gives a degenerate cycle: use its homomorphism lift as the dilation and P=1. Different cpc lifts are handled by the path just proved. Complementing P gives the inverse class: the sum of the two compression Busby maps is, under K=PK⊕(1−P)K, the split map qπ, because its off-diagonal blocks are compact. In the odd cycle this is precisely F↦−F, the inverse convention0.7. Consequently stable semisplit extensions modulo split summands and these whole homotopies form a group Ext_h^−1(A,K), and both constructions give

\[ \operatorname{Ext}_{h}^{-1}(A,\mathcal K) \cong KK^1(A,\mathbb C). \tag{453} \]

The subscript h makes the homotopy convention explicit. This proof is not a claim that all nonsplit extensions of an arbitrary nonnuclear algebra are semisplit or invertible. The analytical extension group used here is this invertible, stable semisplit group, with its entire homotopy convention.

E4. The other parity and the native source convention

Let SA=C0(R)⊗A in the positive physical coordinate order. Section 0.18/0.20 give both actual suspension Bott products; write b_A∈KK^1(A,SA) and d_A∈KK^1(SA,A) for the native parity pair. Their two products are 1, with the ordered positive C1 reductions fixed before reduction. For η∈KK^0(A,ℂ), d_A·η∈KK^1(SA,ℂ) has the compression extension of E1. Its inverse is extension cycle followed on the left by b_A. Associativity and both Bott products prove both inverses. Thus set

\[ K^{\rm an}_1(A)=\operatorname{Ext}_{h}^{-1}(A,\mathcal K), \qquad K^{\rm an}_0(A)=\operatorname{Ext}_{h}^{-1}(SA,\mathcal K). \tag{454} \]

Equations (453)–(454) identify these full groups with KK^j(A,ℂ) for j=1,0. The normalization E1, the actual dilation and both suspension inverses specify their signs and parity. They preserve all classes and torsion. Precomposing a Busby map by a homomorphism agrees with precomposing its dilation cycle, so these identifications are natural.
